title: 'EU-Malaysia trade deal: Jangan jejaskan produk perubatan mampu milik dan hak petani / Don’t put affordable medicines, farmers’ rights at risk
body: '[ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Persatuan Pengguna Pulau Pinang (CAP) dan 40 pertubuhan masyarakat sivil Malaysia yang lain menggesa kerajaan Malaysia supaya menolak tuntutan hak harta intelek oleh Kesatuan Eropah (EU) yang melangkaui kewajipan Malaysia di bawah Perjanjian WTO mengenai Aspek Hak Harta Intelek Berkaitan Perdagangan (TRIPS). Bersama-sama pertubuhan-pertubuhan ini, CAP telah mengemukakan surat kepada Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, memberi amaran bahawa tuntutan TRIPS-plus oleh EU ini boleh menjejaskan akses kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, melemahkan industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan Malaysia, menyekat hak petani serta mengancam keselamatan makanan. Memandangkan pusingan terkini rundingan Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Malaysia-EU sedang berlangsung dari 21 hingga 25 September 2026, kerajaan mestilah memastikan komitmen perdagangan tidak menyekat keupayaan Malaysia untuk melindungi kesihatan awam serta memelihara kepentingan petani dan pengguna. CAP amat bimbang mengenai cadangan EU berkaitan eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, pelanjutan tempoh paten, rahsia perdagangan, penguatkuasaan hak harta intelek, reka bentuk perindustrian dan perlindungan varieti tumbuhan. Langkah-langkah TRIPS-plus ini boleh melanjutkan perlindungan monopoli, melambatkan persaingan ubat generik serta meningkatkan kos bagi pengguna dan sistem penjagaan kesihatan awam. Harga ubat yang lebih tinggi Cadangan EU bagi melanjutkan tempoh paten sehingga lima tahun akan memanjangkan tempoh monopoli farmaseutikal melebihi tempoh paten 20 tahun yang ditetapkan di bawah TRIPS. Apabila digabungkan dengan peluasan eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, peruntukan sebegini boleh melambatkan kemasukan ubat generik yang mampu milik. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Satu kajian semula pada 2022 terhadap 91 kajian mendapati bahawa monopoli farmaseutikal yang lebih kukuh, yang terhasil daripada peruntukan TRIPS-plus, secara umumnya dikaitkan dengan harga ubat yang lebih tinggi, kelewatan ketersediaan ubat serta peningkatan kos bagi pengguna dan kerajaan. Kajian yang sama menganggarkan bahawa kesan gabungan pelanjutan tempoh paten dan eksklusiviti data di bawah Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Colombia–EU boleh meningkatkan perbelanjaan farmaseutikal Colombia sebanyak $756j pada 2025. Cadangan TRIPS-plus EU juga boleh menjejaskan industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan, yang telah dikenal pasti sebagai sektor penting secara strategik di bawah Pelan Induk Perindustrian Baharu 2030 bagi meningkatkan kemampuan, aksesibiliti dan pengeluaran dalam negara. Malaysia juga merupakan pengimport bersih harta intelek, dengan aliran keluar bersih royalti harta intelek berjumlah kira-kira $2.7bn pada 2024, berbanding penerimaan sebanyak kira-kira $348j. Perlindungan harta intelek yang lebih kukuh dan lebih lama akan meningkatkan aliran keluar royalti serta membebankan pengguna Malaysia, program kesihatan awam dan pengeluar tempatan dengan kos tambahan. “Pada masa belanjawan kesihatan Malaysia telah pun dikurangkan, adalah satu tindakan yang sangat tidak bertanggungjawab bagi kerajaan Malaysia untuk bersetuju dengan cadangan EU yang boleh melonjakkan lagi harga produk perubatan serta menambah beban kewangan kepada rakyat Malaysia dan sistem kesihatan awam yang sedia terbeban,” kata Mohideen Abdul Kader, presiden Persatuan Pengguna-Pengguna Pulau Pinang (CAP). Lindungi hak petani CAP dan 40 pertubuhan masyarakat sivil yang lain turut berasa amat bimbang mengenai cadangan EU yang menuntut Malaysia melindungi varieti tumbuhan selaras dengan Akta 1991 Konvensyen Antarabangsa bagi Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu (Upov). Malaysia sudah pun mempunyai sistem perlindungan varieti tumbuhan sendiri di bawah Akta Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu 2004. Rangka kerja ini melindungi pembiak baka tumbuhan komersial di samping memelihara hak petani untuk menyimpan, menggunakan, menukar dan menjual benih varieti yang dilindungi yang disimpan sendiri. Ia juga mengandungi langkah-langkah perlindungan seperti langkah untuk mencegah biopirasi sumber genetik tumbuhan tempatan, serta memastikan ketersediaan benih pada harga yang berpatutan bagi petani Malaysia. Menyelaraskan sistem Malaysia dengan Upov hanya akan menyumbang kepada penguasaan korporat yang lebih besar dalam sektor benih, dan seterusnya meningkatkan kos benih yang membawa implikasi lebih luas kepada pengguna akibat kenaikan harga makanan, serta menjejaskan keselamatan makanan, kepelbagaian biologi pertanian dan daya tahan sektor pertanian Malaysia. Kepentingan EU adalah untuk meningkatkan akses pasaran bagi syarikat benih Eropah di Malaysia. “Malaysia tidak perlu menerima komitmen TRIPS-plus untuk memuktamadkan perjanjian perdagangan yang bercita-cita tinggi dengan EU,” kata Chee Yoke Ling, pengarah eksekutif Third World Network, salah satu pihak yang turut menandatangani surat kepada perdana menteri itu. “Perjanjian EU dengan India baru-baru ini menunjukkan bahawa adalah mungkin untuk merundingkan perjanjian perdagangan tanpa perlu menyelaraskan dengan Upov 1991 dan bersetuju dengan peruntukan TRIPS-plus seperti pelanjutan tempoh paten, eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, serta kewajipan TRIPS-plus yang lain.” Surat itu menggesa kerajaan untuk: - Menolak semua peruntukan harta intelek (TRIPS-plus yang melangkaui kewajipan WTO Malaysia, termasuk eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, pelanjutan tempoh paten, perlindungan rahsia perdagangan dan reka bentuk perindustrian yang berlebihan, langkah-langkah sempadan harta intelek yang diperluas serta komitmen Upov - Melindungi ruang dasar Malaysia untuk menggunakan pelesenan wajib, penggunaan oleh kerajaan dan langkah-langkah perlindungan kesihatan awam yang lain - Mengekalkan Akta Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu 2004 dan menolak sebarang komitmen untuk menyelaraskan dengan atau menyertai Upov - Memastikan bahawa perjanjian perdagangan bebas itu tidak menjejaskan akses kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, persaingan ubat generik dan biosimilar, industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan Malaysia, hak petani atau daya tahan sistem pertanian - Memastikan ketelusan serta perundingan yang bermakna dengan masyarakat sivil, pertubuhan pengguna, kumpulan pesakit dan petani pekebun kecil sepanjang proses rundingan berlangsung CAP selanjutnya menyatakan bahawa kebimbangan terperinci telah pun dibangkitkan dengan kementerian berkaitan, termasuk melalui surat yang dihantar oleh Third World Network pada 4 Jun dan oleh Forum Kedaulatan Makanan Malaysia pada 19 Jun. Pertubuhan-pertubuhan masyarakat sivil itu menyatakan bahawa sehingga kini mereka masih belum menerima sebarang maklum balas daripada mana-mana kementerian mengenai status rundingan itu. CAP menggesa kerajaan supaya memastikan Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Malaysia-EU tidak mengorbankan akses rakyat Malaysia kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, hak petani, keselamatan makanan, mahupun keupayaan Malaysia untuk melaksanakan dasar-dasar demi kepentingan awam. Perjanjian perdagangan mestilah berteraskan kepentingan awam serta memelihara ruang dasar yang diperlukan bagi pembangunan kesihatan, pertanian dan ekonomi Malaysia dalam jangka masa panjang. Antara pihak yang menandatangani surat itu ialah Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Majlis Aids Malaysia (MAC), Yayasan Aids Malaysia (MAF), Forum Kedaulatan Makanan Malaysia (FKMM) dan Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) – cawangan Malaysia; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia (PPIM); Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM); serta Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September English version EU-Malaysia trade deal must not put affordable medical products, farmers’ rights and food security at risk The Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP) and 40 other Malaysian civil society organisations call on the Malaysian government to reject intellectual property demands by the EU that go beyond Malaysia’s obligations under the World Trade Organization’s on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS). Together with these organizations, CAP has sent a letter to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, warning that these TRIPS-plus demands of the EU could undermine access to affordable medicines, weaken Malaysia’s domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, restrict farmers’ rights and threaten food security. With the latest round of the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement negotiations taking place from 21 to 25 September, the government must ensure that trade commitments do not restrict Malaysia’s ability to protect public health, and safeguard the interests of farmers and consumers. CAP is particularly concerned about the EU’s proposals on data and marketing exclusivity, patent-term extension, trade secrets, intellectual property enforcement, industrial designs and plant variety protection. These TRIPS-plus measures could extend monopoly protection, delay generic competition and increase costs for consumers and the public healthcare system. Higher medicine prices competition The EU’s proposals for patent-term extensions of up to five years would extend pharmaceutical monopolies beyond the 20-year patent term required under TRIPS. Combined with expanded data and marketing exclusivity, such provisions could delay the entry of affordable generic medicines. A 2022 review of 91 studies found that stronger pharmaceutical monopolies created through TRIPS-plus provisions are generally associated with higher drug prices, delayed availability and increased costs for consumers and governments. The same review estimated that the combined impact of patent-term extensions and data exclusivity under the Colombia–EU Free Trade Agreement could increase Colombia’s pharmaceutical spending by $756m in 2025. The EU’s TRIPS-plus proposals can also undermine the domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, which has been identified as strategically important under the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 for improving affordability, accessibility and domestic production. Malaysia is also a net importer of intellectual property, with about $2.7bn in net intellectual property royalty outflows in 2024, compared with around $348m in receipts. Stronger and longer intellectual property protection would increase royalty outflows and impose additional costs on local consumers, public health programmes and domestic manufacturers. “At a time when Malaysia’s health budget has already been cut, it would be deeply irresponsible for the Malaysian government to agree to EU proposals that could further drive up the prices of medical products and place additional financial burdens on the Malaysian people and on an already stretched public health system,” said Mohideen Abdul Kader, president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang. Protect farmers’ rights CAP and the other 40 civil society organisations are also deeply concerned about the EU’s proposal requiring Malaysia to protect plant varieties in accordance with the 1991 Act of the International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (Upov). Malaysia already has its own plant variety protection system under the Protection of New Plant Varieties Act 2004. This framework protects commercial plant breeders while preserving farmers’ rights to save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seeds of protected varieties. It also contains safeguards such as measures to prevent biopiracy of local plant genetic resources, and ensure the availability of seeds at reasonable prices for Malaysian farmers. Aligning Malaysia’s system with Upov will only contribute to greater corporate concentration in the seed sector, and consequently increase the costs of seeds with wider implications for consumers as food prices increase, food security, agrobiodiversity and the resilience of Malaysian agriculture. The EU’s interest is to increase market access for European seed companies in Malaysia. “Malaysia does not need to accept TRIPS-plus commitments to conclude an ambitious EU trade agreement,” said Chee Yoke Ling, the executive director of Third World Network, another signatory to the letter to the prime minister. “Recent EU agreement with India demonstrates that it is possible to negotiate a trade agreement without having to align with Upov 1991 and agree to TRIPS-plus provisions such as patent-term extension, data and marketing exclusivity, and other TRIPS-plus obligations.” The letter calls on the government to: - Reject all TRIPS-plus intellectual property provisions that go beyond Malaysia’s WTO obligations, including data and marketing exclusivity, patent-term extensions, excessive trade-secret and industrial-design protection, expanded intellectual property border measures and Upov commitments - Protect Malaysia’s policy space to use compulsory licensing, government use and other public health safeguards - Maintain the Protection of New Plant Varieties Act 2004 and reject any commitment to align with or accede to Upov - Ensure that the free trade agreement does not undermine access to affordable medicines, generic and biosimilar competition, Malaysia’s domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, farmers’ rights or the resilience of the agricultural system - Ensure transparency and meaningful consultation with civil society, consumer organisations, patient groups and smallholder farmers throughout the negotiations CAP further notes that detailed concerns have already been raised with the relevant ministries, including through letters sent by Third World Network on 4 June and by the Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum on 19 June. The civil society organisations state that, to date, they have not received a response from any ministry concerning the status of the negotiations. CAP urges the government to ensure that the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement does not trade away Malaysians’ access to affordable medicines, farmers’ rights, food security or Malaysia’s ability to pursue public interest policies. Trade agreements must serve the public interest and preserve the policy space needed for Malaysia’s long-term health, agricultural and economic development. Signatories to the letter include the Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Malaysian Aids Council, Malaysian Aids Foundation, Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum, Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières Malaysian chapter; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia; Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth) – SAM; and Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September Mohideen Abdul Kader is the president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP). The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

CAP urges the government to ensure that the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement does not trade away Malaysians’ access to affordable medicines, farmers’ rights, food security or Malaysia’s ability to pursue public interest policies. Trade agreements must serve the public interest and preserve the policy space needed for Malaysia’s long-term health, agricultural and economic development. Signatories to the letter include the Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Malaysian Aids Council, Malaysian Aids Foundation, Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum, Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières Malaysian chapter; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia; Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth) – SAM; and Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September Mohideen Abdul Kader is the president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP). title: 'RHB Umum Penyelarasan Caj DuitNow QR Peniaga – Bermula 26 Oktober Ini – Rnggt
body: 'Pemegang akaun peniaga RHB Bank tidak lama lagi bakal berdepan dengan penyelarasan kadar caj pemprosesan atau Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) bagi transaksi DuitNow QR yang diproses menerusi saluran rasmi bank tersebut mulai 26 Oktober ini. Berdasarkan notis pengumuman terbaharu daripada RHB Bank, penyelarasan kadar itu dilaksanakan selaras dengan perkembangan lanskap pembayaran digital tempatan serta keperluan perkhidmatan berterusan. Namun, caj baharu ini hanya terpakai kepada perkhidmatan perniagaan dan tidak melibatkan transaksi pembayaran oleh pengguna awam. Menerusi pelaksaan terbaharu ini, caj pemprosesan bagi perniagaan yang menggunakan Akaun Simpanan, Akaun Semasa, mahupun dompet digital ditetapkan pada kadar 0.35% daripada keseluruhan nilai transaksi. Manakala bagi transaksi pembayaran DuitNow QR yang dibuat menggunakan kad kredit pula, kadar caj yang bakal dikenakan adalah sebanyak 0.60%. Sebagai contoh, bagi setiap bayaran RM100 yang diterima daripada pelanggan menerusi akaun bank atau dompet digital, peniaga akan dikenakan potongan caj sebanyak RM0.35 (menerima RM99.65 bersih), manakala bayaran RM100 menerusi kad kredit pula akan dipotong sebanyak RM0.60 (menerima RM99.40 bersih). Penyesuaian struktur kadar ini merangkumi transaksi yang diproses menerusi tiga saluran utama iaitu peranti terminal kad, DuitNow QR Sound Box/Sound Box+, serta perkhidmatan Reflex Mobile dan kad perniagaan. Langkah penyelarasan kadar MDR RHB secara berperingkat ini selari dengan penamatan pengecualian caj di peringkat rasmi sebelum ini. Pihak RHB menjelaskan bahawa pelaksanaan kadar baharu ini membolehkan mereka untuk terus menyokong keperluan operasi perniagaan peniaga dengan kualiti perkhidmatan yang konsisten dan mampan. Peniaga yang memerlukan penjelasan lanjut disaran untuk menghubungi cawangan RHB Bank yang berdekatan.

title: 'Foreign selling on Bursa extends to second week, TNB, Maybank and RHB lead outflows
body: 'FOREIGN institutions remained net sellers of Malaysian equities for a second consecutive week, recording RM799.9 million in net outflows for the week ended Oct 2, with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) and RHB Bank Bhd bearing the brunt of the selling.   According to MBSB Research’s weekly fund flow report released today, foreign institutions were net sellers on all five trading days, with the largest outflow recorded on Wednesday at RM228.4 million.   Stock-level data showed TNB recorded the largest net foreign outflow at RM278.1 million, followed by Maybank at RM159.3 million and RHB Bank at RM135.9 million.

title: 'CIMB Share Buyback, Market Watching
body: 'CIMB Group Holdings Bhd’s ongoing share buyback programme could mark a significant shift in how Malaysian banks manage excess capital, although investor acceptance will depend on how the programme is balanced against expectations for special dividends, according to MBSB Research.  The research house maintained its Buy call on CIMB but trimmed its target price to RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times.  MBSB said CIMB has been buying back shares daily since Sept 21, acquiring 20.76 million shares for about RM163 million, implying a weighted average purchase price of RM7.85 per share.  The shares, equivalent to about 0.192% of CIMB’s issued share capital, are currently being held as treasury shares and have not been cancelled.  The buybacks form part of CIMB’s RM2 billion capital return programme, of which RM700 million has already been distributed through special dividends.  If the remaining RM1.3 billion were used entirely for share repurchases, MBSB estimated CIMB could buy back around 1.5% of its total share base.  The research house said the programme is aimed at improving earnings per share, return on equity and dividend per share, particularly as CIMB remains slightly behind its FY2026 ROE target.  Share Buybacks Face Malaysian Investor Test  MBSB cautioned, however, that share buybacks have historically received a mixed response in Malaysia, where many local investors tend to favour direct cash dividends.  This differs from markets such as Singapore, where share repurchases are more established as a capital-management tool.  MBSB said CIMB’s relatively high level of foreign investor participation could help support acceptance of the strategy, although market expectations for further special dividends remain high.  The research house noted that the impact of buybacks would also be less permanent if the treasury shares are eventually reissued rather than cancelled.  Its scenario analysis showed that a 1.5% share buyback could lift FY2027 forecast EPS to 75.7 sen from 74.5 sen, ROE to 11.1% from 10.9%, and DPS to 49.2 sen from 48.4 sen, assuming a 65% dividend payout.  Under that scenario, MBSB estimated the implied target price could rise to RM9.46.  Capital Return Could Be Revised Higher  MBSB said there is also a possibility CIMB could eventually revise its RM2 billion capital return programme higher if additional capital becomes available.  Potential sources could include capital repatriation from subsidiaries, restructuring of less profitable businesses and changes arising from Basel requirements.  The research house said the market will be watching whether CIMB’s approach succeeds, as it could encourage other larger banks to consider similar capital-management strategies.  MBSB identified Public Bank and RHB Bank as potential candidates, given their mature dividend payout levels, relatively strong capital positions and exposure to foreign investors.  Earnings Outlook Remains Supportive  MBSB expects CIMB’s FY2027 core net profit to reach RM8.05 billion, rising 4% from FY2026, with ROE at 10.9% and dividend yield at 6.2%.  The research house continues to view CIMB positively on the back of strong non-interest income growth, wealth management momentum, cost discipline and improving profitability.  However, it flagged potential net interest margin compression, dividend disappointment and weakness in the Indonesian business as key downside risks.  At RM7.79 as of Sept 30, CIMB was trading at about 1.13 times FY2027 forecast book value, with MBSB projecting a total return of about 24.3%, including dividends.

title: 'Mahkamah putus 23 Okt permohonan injunksi Maritime Network terhadap RHB
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur menetapkan 23 Okt untuk memutuskan permohonan injunksi sebuah syarikat perkapalan bagi menghalang RHB Bank Berhad daripada menutup dua akaun lama milik syarikat itu sementara menunggu penyelesaian saman penuhnya.   Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman, Elesabet Paya Wan, menetapkan tarikh itu selepas mendengar hujahan peguam P Taneswaran yang mewakili Maritime Network Sdn Bhd dan peguam bank berkenaan, Gan Khong Aik.   Terdahulu, Taneswaran berhujah pihak bank gagal menunjukkan sama ada plaintif, Maritime Network, telah melanggar mana-mana terma atau keperluan yang boleh menyebabkan akaunnya ditutup.

title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.   Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.   Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

title: 'RHB tumbles 9% as foreign selling pressure persists
body: 'FOREIGN investors kept up the selling pressure on Malaysian equities for another week, with RHB Bank Bhd among the hardest hit after losing close to 9% over the past fortnight as the benchmark index slipped below 1,700 points.   RHB fell from RM8.68 on Aug 28 to RM7.90 on Sept 11, down 78 sen or about 9%, amid heavy selling pressure. The counter extended its decline in early trade today, falling to RM7.75.   Foreign investors remained net sellers for the week ended Sept 11, marking the sixth consecutive week of net foreign outflows.

title: 'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia
body: 'Trending F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia F1 Bahrain GP di Sepang dijangka menarik 300,000 pengunjung termasuk 50,000 pelancong asing serta menjana impak ekonomi RM1.3 bilion. Intipati berita - 300,000 pengunjung disasarkan hadir ke SIC, termasuk 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa. - F1 dijangka menjana impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion kepada Malaysia. - MOTAC & Tourism Malaysia menyediakan pakej pelancongan untuk menggalakkan pelancong asing tinggal lebih lama di Malaysia. - F1 turut menjadi platform mempromosikan pelancongan, budaya dan seni Malaysia sempena Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027. Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur.

Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur.

title: 'Diplomasi Sukan Anwar Letakkan Malaysia Kembali Di Persada Global – Penganalisis
body: 'Pendekatan Perdana Menteri Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yang memanfaatkan sukan sebagai platform diplomasi, aktiviti ekonomi dan penjenamaan negara membantu meletakkan semula Malaysia di pentas sukan global, menurut penganalisis. Felow Kanan Global Peace Institute Profesor Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam berkata sejak beberapa bulan lepas, Malaysia telah menunjukkan betapa acara sukan global dapat dimanfaatkan bukan sahaja untuk menghiburkan orang ramai, tetapi juga memperkukuh hubungan antarabangsa, menjana aktiviti ekonomi dan mewujudkan rasa keterujaan di seluruh negara. “Sukan sering dianggap sebagai hiburan, tetapi bagi kerajaan, bidang itu juga boleh menjadi diplomasi, dasar ekonomi dan penjenamaan negara yang digabungkan menjadi satu,” katanya dalam kenyataan, hari ini. Formula Satu (F1) kembali ke Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) selepas sembilan tahun dan usaha Malaysia untuk memastikan akses kepada siaran Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 baru-baru ini, menunjukkan bahawa sukan juga dapat dimanfaatkan untuk memperkukuh penglibatan antarabangsa negara. Mohd Mizan berkata penganjuran F1 Grand Prix (GP) Gulf Air Bahrain di negara ini selama tiga hari hingga hari ini, menunjukkan dimensi antarabangsa diplomasi sukan, selepas GP Bahrain tidak dapat diteruskan di lokasi asalnya berikutan keadaan geopolitik di Asia Barat. Beliau berkata pengaturan itu melangkaui transaksi komersial yang melibatkan litar lumba kerana perkara itu dimudahkan dalam rangka hubungan antara Malaysia dengan Bahrain, dengan sokongan Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim dan Raja Bahrain Raja Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Putera Mahkota merangkap Perdana Menteri Bahrain Putera Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa turut berangkat ke Malaysia dan bertemu dengan Anwar pada hujung minggu perlumbaan berkenaan. Mohd Mizan berkata kehadiran Anwar pada sesi kelayakan di Sepang, melawat ke pit Mercedes-AMG Petronas dan penglibatan dalam majlis resepsi yang dianjurkan Putera Salman menunjukkan bahawa acara sukan itu dapat mewujudkan platform untuk penglibatan diplomatik. “Sukan mewujudkan platform diplomatik. Pemimpin bertemu, hubungan dua hala diperkukuh dan Malaysia diletakkan di hadapan khalayak global bukan melalui sidang kemuncak rasmi, tetapi menerusi satu daripada pertunjukan sukan yang paling dikenali di dunia,” katanya. Maklum balas orang ramai terhadap kembalinya F1 juga, katanya, sama penting dengan kira-kira 95,000 tiket tiga hari terjual pada akhir September dan SIC menjangkakan penjualan mencecah kira-kira 100,000 yang bakal menjadi jualan tiket tertinggi yang direkodkan untuk perlumbaan yang diadakan di litar tersebut. Beliau berkata acara itu juga menjana limpahan ekonomi yang ketara, dengan Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menganggarkan acara sukan tersebut mampu menarik kira-kira 300,000 pelancong termasuk sekitar 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa, manakala Hong Leong Bank Research mengunjurkan impak ekonomi kira-kira RM1.3 bilion melalui pelancongan sukan dan perbelajaan pelawat asing. “F1 tidak hanya memberikan manfaat kepada litar. Pengunjung berbelanja di hotel, restoran, pengangkutan, peruncitan dan pelancongan. Liputan televisyen membawa imej Malaysia ke seluruh dunia. Pasukan, penaja, wartawan dan pemimpin korporat global tiba di negara ini,” katanya. Berhubung sukan bola sepak, Mohd Mizan berkata keputusan kerajaan untuk memastikan Malaysia mempunyai akses kepada Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 mewakili dimensi domestik diplomasi sukan, berikutan bola sepak terus menjadi satu daripada sukan yang paling diikuti ramai di negara ini. RTM dan Unifi TV dilantik selaku penyiar rasmi, dengan kesemua 104 perlawanan dapat ditonton menerusi platform yang mengambil bahagian, manakala kerajaan memperuntukkan RM26.2 juta untuk memperoleh hak penyiaran, di samping kerjasama strategik dengan sektor swasta yang membantu meluaskan akses dan pengedaran, katanya. Beliau berkata akses kepada Piala Dunia melalui saluran yang sah dan mudah diakses mewakili satu bentuk keterangkuman sosial kerana acara sukan utama dapat mewujudkan pengalaman bersama merentasi kaum, umur, geografi dan pendapatan. “Semasa perlawanan bola sepak utama, restoran mamak, ruang tamu di rumah, dewan komuniti dan kawasan tontonan awam menjadi ruang yang dikongsi bersama-sama rakyat Malaysia,” katanya. Mohd Mizan berkata pendekatan Anwar menunjukkan bahawa diplomasi hari ini berlangsung jauh melangkaui bilik persidangan rasmi, dengan Malaysia menggunakan F1 dan FIFA untuk mendekatkan dunia dengan rakyatnya sambil memperkukuh kedudukan di pentas sukan antarabangsa. “Kadangkala, diplomasi berlaku melalui rundingan dua hala. Ada kalanya diplomasi terjadi menerusi bola sepak dan kadang-kadang, pada kelajuan 300 kilometer sejam di sekitar Sepang,” katanya. — BERNAMA.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank Wins Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards In M'sia
body: 'Hong Leong Bank has been named Malaysia’s winner at the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026, taking the prize in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category. The bank was recognized for modernizing a critical online business application by moving away from a monolithic architecture to a containerized environment powered by Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. Hong Leong Bank’s Modernization Efforts Hong Leong Bank identified scalability limitations and manual processes within a legacy application architecture as key obstacles to its digital banking ambitions. To address this, the bank transitioned the application from a monolithic framework into a containerized environment using Red Hat OpenShift, while also deploying Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to modernize its existing database infrastructure. The deployment unified virtual machines and containers onto a single common platform, reducing the complexity of managing separate infrastructure stacks. Manual virtual machine patching for containerized workloads was also eliminated as part of the transition. The most measurable outcome from the shift is a dramatic reduction in software deployment cycles, which dropped from months to weeks – applications can now scale dynamically during traffic spikes, giving the bank the agility to deliver new digital banking features at a faster pace without compromising reliability. William Streitberg, Chief Information and Technology Officer at Hong Leong Bank, noted that updating infrastructure requires understanding the right fit for each operation, and that Red Hat has provided a common foundation for both existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing new capabilities to be introduced faster while maintaining the reliability customers expect. Daniel Aw, Vice President and General Manager for APAC at Red Hat, said that enterprise technology success is increasingly about how effectively solutions work together rather than how many new technologies an organisation adopts. He highlighted that this year’s award winners are building open, flexible foundations that allow them to innovate on their own terms. Red Hat positions open source as a response to growing complexity in AI, hybrid cloud, and automation strategies, where organisations need the flexibility to choose technologies best suited to their specific business requirements. Pokdepinion: Cutting deployment cycles from months to weeks is going to net them plenty of benefits down the line.

title: 'AKPK Celebrates 20 Years with Strategic Partnership Program
body: 'Accra:The Credit Counselling and Debt Management Agency (AKPK) marked its 20th anniversary by hosting the 'Rencah Kita Pelbagai Rasa, Satu Makna' programme, aimed at strengthening relationships with strategic partners. According to BERNAMA News Agency, AKPK's chief executive officer, Azman Hasim, highlighted that the cooking challenge, organized in collaboration with M Resort and Hotel, included 30 agencies such as financial service providers, media partners, and other strategic partners. The event symbolized the blending of diverse strengths and expertise to enhance financial resilience among Malaysians. Azman emphasized that the agency's anniversary reflects the collective success of various parties working towards a unified goal. He likened the impact of their work to a well-prepared dish, underscoring the importance of understanding each component's role in achieving meaningful outcomes. He also noted that each AKPK undertaking involves real people with lives that need support and rebuilding. The event underscored the importance of strategic partnerships in providing the necessary guidance and confidence to help individuals overcome financial challenges. The primary focus of the day was the relationships and communication fostered through the challenge, rather than the competition itself. Azman reiterated that while participants have different perspectives, they share a common goal of improving the wellbeing of Malaysians. The annual event, which introduces new activities each year, serves as a platform to honor the strategic partners that have contributed to AKPK's success over the past two decades. Notable participants included Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), CIMB Bank Berhad (CIMB), Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, and AmBank (M) Bhd.

The event underscored the importance of strategic partnerships in providing the necessary guidance and confidence to help individuals overcome financial challenges. The primary focus of the day was the relationships and communication fostered through the challenge, rather than the competition itself. Azman reiterated that while participants have different perspectives, they share a common goal of improving the wellbeing of Malaysians. The annual event, which introduces new activities each year, serves as a platform to honor the strategic partners that have contributed to AKPK's success over the past two decades. Notable participants included Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), CIMB Bank Berhad (CIMB), Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, and AmBank (M) Bhd.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends slightly higher as technology counters dominate trading
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Bursa Malaysia staged a slight recovery on Friday as bargain-hunting emerged following a recent sharp sell-off, said an analyst. However, the rebound lacked momentum as broader Asian markets remained under pressure ahead of key United States labour market data. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.51 points, or 0.03 per cent, to 1,630.87 from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The benchmark index, which opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, moved between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 throughout the trading session. Market breadth turned positive with gainers leading losers 585 to 541, while 558 counters were unchanged, 1,089 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover climbed to 4.23 billion units, worth RM2.70 billion, from 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion on Thursday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the recent sell-off had brought valuations of selected blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, which could encourage gradual accumulation and provide some downside support. However, he said investors continued to adopt a defensive stance as bond yields and crude oil prices remained elevated. “As for the local bourse, we remain cautious despite today’s rebound, as external headwinds are likely to keep market volatility elevated,” Thong told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose seven sen to RM10.02, Public Bank fell one sen to RM4.66, CIMB eased four sen to RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional firmed up six sen to RM12.96, and IHH Healthcare added 10 sen to RM7.80. In active trade, Zetrix AI erased five sen to 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources remained unchanged at 18 sen, JCY International jumped 10.5 sen to 66 sen, V.S Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and PUC went up one sen to 4.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries rose RM1.28 to RM42.40, UWC rallied 47 sen to RM7.57, Vitrox bounced 46 sen to RM10.46, United Plantations gained 42 sen to RM31.38, and UMS Integration improved 38 sen to RM9.03. Top losers were led by Nestle, which reduced 48 sen to RM89.52; Kuala Lumpur Kepong fell 42 sen to RM21; Enra trimmed 25.5 sen to 72.5 sen, while Allianz Malaysia and Hong Leong Bank both shaved off 20 sen to RM20.80 and RM22.64, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 122.94 points to 17,481.93, the FBM Emas Index added 27.04 points to 12,170.57, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 24.52 points to 11,957.68. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 47.31 points to 12,060.32, and the FBM ACE Index improved 46.49 points to 5,529.46. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.79 points to 178.52, while the Energy Index shaved off 1.98 points to 833.03. The Financial Services Index eased 20.40 points to 19,040.51, and the Plantation Index grew 29.97 points to 9,056.55. The Main Market volume increased to 2.67 billion units worth RM2.34 billion from 1.82 billion units valued at RM2.42 billion on Thursday. Warrant turnover soared to 973.40 million units worth RM160.21 million from 618.78 million units valued at RM72.71 million previously. The ACE Market volume eased to 593.05 million units valued at RM205.21 million from 650.13 million units worth RM226.92 million yesterday. Meanwhile, consumer products and services counters accounted for 241.01 million shares traded on the Main Market, industrial products and services (266.57 million), construction (183.37 million), technology (1.41 billion), financial services (50.26 million), property (152.37 million), plantation (19.73 million), real estate investment trusts (15.78 million), closed-end fund (214,200), energy (99.69 million), healthcare (103.06 million), telecommunications and media (28.89 million), transportation and logistics (47.35 million), utilities (46.61 million), and business trusts (119,600). — Bernama

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 22 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI edged up 0.1% to 1,666.9 points on Monday, snapping a threesession losing streak, as bargain hunting in selected blue-chip counters lifted the index amid easing concerns over the West Asia conflict and retreating oil prices. Energy (+3.0%), Utilities (+1.9%) and Transportation & Logistics (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.4%), YTL Power (+0.3%) and Petronas Dagangan (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 654 to 552, and 517 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday, supported by renewed strength in technology and semiconductor stocks, easing oil prices and improved sentiment ahead of the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI led regional gains, rising 1.7%, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.2%), Taiwan's TAIEX (+1.1%) and China's Shanghai Composite (+1.0%), while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, chipmakers led the gains, with Samsung Electronics rising 5.0% after US semiconductor stocks rallied, while semiconductor exports surged 259% YoY to USD34.1 bn in the first 20 days of September, reinforcing expectations of strong chip demand and earnings. In China, sentiment was supported by gains in technology and healthcare stocks, while the PBOC maintained its key lending rates and investors awaited the Trump-Xi meeting. European stocks closed firmly higher on Monday, supported by lower sovereign yields and easing ongoing pressures from an adverse macroeconomic backdrop. The Euro STOXX 50 gained 1.3% to 6,318 and the STOXX Europe 600 rose 1.0% to 642. Natural gas and fuel prices pulled back following the weekend amid signs that GCC nations are chasing diplomatic ways with Iran to restart tanker flows through the Persian Gulf. The drop in yields aided the outlook of credit and supported banks, with UniCredit, Nordea, and BBVA adding between 3.2% and 2%. Lastly, a global rally for the AI infrastructure sector supported Infineon with a 4.3% jump, while ASML added 2.5%. US stocks rallied on Monday, supported by falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields, while optimism over the upcoming Trump-Xi summit further lifted sentiment. The Nasdaq CI surged 2.26%, while the S&P 500 and Dow gained 1.49% and 0.71%, respectively. Meta jumped 11.3% on optimism over its AI offering, Muse, while AMD and Intel surged 10% and 12.1%, respectively. Investors now await earnings from AutoZone and KB Home, along with speeches from Federal Reserve officials. US: Treasury Yields Edge Down 4.95% on Monday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell 4bps to 4.95% on Monday, as traders started the new week with another decline in oil prices, amid hopes that diplomatic efforts could lead to a resolution to the conflict with Iran. Oil prices have now fallen for four consecutive sessions, easing some concerns over renewed inflationary pressures (Trading Economics) US: Gold Slips on Dollar Strength Gold prices edged lower toward $4,350 on Monday, pressured by a stronger US dollar and profit-taking after last week’s rally, while investors continued to monitor developments in the Middle East. Bullion reached its highest level in more than a week on Friday as falling oil prices eased concerns over prolonged inflationary pressures. Oil prices extended their decline at the start of the week as investors looked for signs of diplomatic progress on the Iran conflict around this week’s UN meetings, although tensions remained elevated as Iran and the US exchanged fresh threats on Sunday. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Decline as Supply Concerns Ease Crude oil held below $96 per barrel on Tuesday after falling for four consecutive sessions, pressured by easing supply concerns in the Middle East and growing diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. President Donald Trump is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly in New York later today and could meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines. Trump is also expected to hold discussions with other Gulf nations and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. (Trading Economics) US: AI adoption is driving hiring, but mostly for senior roles Companies using artificial intelligence are adding more jobs than those that are not but those gains sharply favour senior employees over junior workers, according to a new study spanning 41 countries. The number of employees in senior positions rose by 6.7% over five years at companies adopting AI while junior employment declined 3% in the same period, researchers Bharat Chandar of Stanford University and Bouke Klein Teeselink of King’s College London said in a paper released on Monday. (Bloomberg) US: Fed's Kashkari says inflation is still too high in 'all aspects' of US economy Minneapolis Federal Reserve president Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices. "So even if we strip out energy, which is really volatile, and strip out food — they matter a lot — but in terms of where the economy is going, inflation is still too high," Kashkari told Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures. (Reuters) US: Housing costs rise further out of reach ahead of mid-terms Barely six weeks out from the midterm elections, housing costs that many Americans have long said are too high are looking even more out of reach. The latest blow for consumers came Thursday, when Freddie Mac reported that rates for 30-year mortgages climbed to 6.95%, the highest since January 2025, when President Donald Trump returned to office. That report emerged after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, crushing any hopes that borrowing costs will come down soon. (Bloomberg) US: New data centres worth US$68 billion disrupted in US, data show Opposition to data centres continues to mount in the US. That is according to research group Data Center Watch, which said some 45 data centre projects worth US$68 billion (RM277.28 billion) were blocked or delayed by local pushback between April and June this year. Communities across the country are now pushing through moratoriums on new construction, often before developers can apply for permissions. (Bloomberg) US: EM investors are favouring local bonds as dollar debt lags Emerging-market investors are for now sticking with local-currency sovereign debt as surging Treasury yields dim the appeal of dollardenominated developing-nation bonds. Behind the strategy are attractive valuations and the potential to profit from carry trades, where investors borrow in low-yielding currencies to invest in higher-yielding assets. (Bloomberg) US: ECB launches key link between blockchain and euro payment system The European Central Bank on Monday began letting banks settle tokenised wholesale transactions in central-bank money while continuing efforts to develop a digital euro for consumers by the end of the decade. The so-called Pontes project links blockchain markets with the euro area’s existing payment systems. It will eventually be replaced by a longer-term solution known as Appia, for which a blueprint should be ready in 2028. (Bloomberg) CN: Yuan hits fresh multi-year peak as China's central bank eases curb ahead of Trump-Xi summit China's yuan strengthened to more than a 3-1/2-year high against the US dollar on Monday as the central bank softened its curb on currency appreciation ahead of the meeting this week between the leaders of China and the US.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng concluded talks in New York on Sunday, laying the groundwork for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to consider at their summit from Sept 23-25. (Reuters) SK: Early exports maintain strong momentum on chip boom South Korea’s exports continued to grow at a solid pace in early September as global demand for artificial-intelligence supported semiconductor shipments and the broader trade-dependent economy. Exports adjusted for working-day differences rose 89.8% from a year earlier in the first 20 days of September, according to customs office data released Monday. That compared with an initially reported 61.5% increase during the same period in August. (Bloomberg) MY: Nearly two-thirds of Malaysians make RM2,200 or less a month in 2025 - official data Nearly two-thirds of Malaysia’s wage earners were in semi- and low-skilled jobs in 2025, with median monthly wages of RM2,223 or less, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). Semi-skilled workers, who accounted for 55.6% of wage earners, had a median monthly wage of RM2,223, while low-skilled workers, who make up 7.8% of wage earners, earned RM1,758. Skilled workers, by comparison, earned a median RM5,057. Skilled workers make up 36.6% of total wage recipients. (The Edge) MY: Malaysians' average monthly salary up 4% to RM3,803 in 2025 - DOSM The average monthly salary and wage of Malaysians increased by 4.1% to RM3,803 in 2025, compared with RM3,652 the previous year, according to the Salaries and Wages Survey Report 2025 published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) on Monday. At the same time, the median monthly salary and wage increased by 5.3 % to RM2,940 from RM2,793 in 2024. (Berrnama) MY: REIT managers call for return of withholding tax relief in Budget 2027 The Malaysian REIT Managers Association (MRMA) hopes the withholding tax break on real estate investment trusts (REITs) dividends will be restored in Budget 2027. AmFIRST Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) manager and chief executive officer Chong Hong Chuon told reporters after its annual general meeting and extraordinary general meeting that the association had submitted its requests to the government, including a review of the tax treatment for REIT distributions. (Berrnama) AAGB: Malaysia wins best low-cost airline award for 17th year as it renews operating certificate AirAsia Malaysia, the carrier operated by AirAsia Group Bhd, was recognised as the World’s Best Low-Cost Airline for the 17th consecutive year at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards in London last Friday.The latest win comes as the airline marks 25 years of operations. (The Edge) INSPACE: Bags RM35 mil subcontract for renovation works Interior fit-out firm Inspace Creation Bhd has won a subcontract of RM34.75 million to undertake renovation works on commercial properties. In a Bursa Malaysia filing on Monday, the group stated that its indirectly wholly owned subsidiary, IDPM Builder Sdn Bhd, had accepted a letter of award for the project from an undisclosed customer on Monday. The company said it could not disclose the identity of the main contractor as well as the location of the project and specific details of the subcontract due to confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Hits four-year high after slew of good news Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd, hit a four-year high on Monday in a sudden spike in its share price, which came amid a slew of positive developments, including the renewal of a 10-year product supply deal with Shell Malaysia two weeks ago. The spike comes as brent crude futures fell to a week’s low of US$101.7 (RM415.06) a barrel. (The Edge) PWRWELL: Secures RM190m orders to supply low voltage switchgear for data centre in Johor Powerwell Holdings Bhd said on Monday it has secured two contracts worth RM190.42 million for the supply of low-voltage switchgear and related equipment for a data centre project in Johor. The electrical equipment manufacturer said its wholly owned unit, Powerwell International Sdn Bhd, will be supplying the equipment to a multinational technology corporation specialising in data centres. (The Edge) DIALOG: Gets PETRONAS approval for US$81m RAJA Cluster development plan Dialog Group Bhd said its RAJA Cluster small field asset production sharing contract (PSC) has received approval from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) for an US$81 million (RM330.29 million) field development and abandonment plan. In a bourse filing on Monday, Dialog said the final investment decision for the plan was approved by PETRONAS through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM). (The Edge) EFORCE: Proposes RM11 mil private placement to fund working capital as TS Wong hit by selldowns Excel Force MSC Bhd, one of the companies linked to businessman Wong Thean Soon, has proposed a private placement to raise up to RM10.98 million for working capital and free up funds for a software project. The financial technology solutions provider plans to issue up to 60.99 million new shares, representing 10% of its existing issued share capital, to third-party investors to be identified later, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia on Monday. (The Edge) WINSTAR: Plans RM300 million sukuk for investments, land acquisition, refinancing Winstar Capital Bhd proposes to issue a RM300 million sukuk to finance investments and land acquisition, as well as to refinance existing loans. The group, which lodged the sukuk murabahah programme with the Securities Commission Malaysia on Monday, said proceeds will also be used to defray issuance expenses and for working capital. (The Edge) SPSETIA: Launches 100-acre Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines S P Setia Bhd officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines in Kepala Batas, Penang — marking a significant milestone in the group's placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. According to a press statement on Sept 21, the launch was graced by Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, alongside state representatives, government agencies, strategic partners, invited guests, residents and members of the public. (The Edge) KGB: To collaborate with Tata Group's unit on Gujarat semiconductor fabrication facility Kelington Group Bhd has entered into a collaboration with electronics and semiconductor manufacturer Tata Electronics to advance the development of the latter’s semiconductor fabrication facility (Fab) in Dholera, Gujarat. Kelington said under the agreement dated Sept 18, the group will support the Tata Group’s unit in infrastructure and system deployment for the facility. (The Edge) PEKAT: Unit to lease 470 acres in Sungai Petani for 24 years for renewable energy activities Pekat Group Bhd said on Monday that it will lease about 470 acres of land in Sungai Petani, Kedah for renewable energy activities, including the development of solar photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage systems. In a bourse filing, the engineering services firm said its wholly owned unit Pekat Teknologi Sdn Bhd had entered into a conditional lease agreement with an unnamed company to lease the land. The company cited a confidentiality obligation for its reason to not name the lessor. (The Edge) GAMUDA: JV secures RM1.8 bil Western Sydney road upgrade contract Gamuda Bhd and Australian construction group BMD Constructions Pty Ltd have secured a A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) contract to upgrade two roads in Western Sydney. Transport for New South Wales awarded the Elizabeth Drive Upgrade-Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 project to the Gamuda-BMD Joint Venture (GBJV), which is equally owned by both parties, Gamuda said in a bourse filing on Monday. Gamuda’s 50% share of the contract is expected to generate A$312 million, or about RM908 million, in revenue. The project commenced on Monday and is targeted for completion in 2030. (The Edge) CTOS: Appoints Najib's daughter Putri Norlisa as independent director Putri Norlisa Najib, the eldest daughter of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, has joined CTOS Digital Bhd as an independent non-executive director. The 45-year-old lawyer's board appointment will take effect on Sept 25, according to a bourse filing by CTOS. She is one of three children from Najib's first marriage to Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar. Putri Norlisa is currently the joint managing partner of Adnan Sundra & Low, a position she has held since 2023. (The Edge) SSB8: Unit wins RM40 mil electrical works job for Nilai data centre Southern Score Builders Bhd has won a RM40 million subcontract for electrical works at a data centre project in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan. According to a bourse filing, Southern Score Builders said the letter of award was given to its 51%-owned subsidiary SJEE Engineering Sdn Bhd from an unnamed local construction company on Monday. SJEE will be responsible for the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of electrical works, as well as maintenance and warranty services. (The Edge) STRAITS: Proposes capital reduction to wipe out RM90 million in losses Straits Energy Resources Bhd has proposed a share capital reduction to eliminate RM90 million in accumulated losses. Based on the latest unaudited results, the proposed share capital reduction would eliminate the group's RM39.17 million accumulated losses as of June 30, 2026 – resulting in retained earnings of RM50.83 million, before taking into account the estimated RM165,000 expenses related to the exercise as well as the foreign currency translation reserve of RM4.05 million, the group said in a bourse filing on Monday (Sept 21). 'Daily Newswatch - 22 Sep 2026

'The FBM KLCI edged up 0.1% to 1,666.9 points on Monday, snapping a threesession losing streak, as bargain hunting in selected blue-chip counters lifted the index amid easing concerns over the West Asia conflict and retreating oil prices. Energy (+3.0%), Utilities (+1.9%) and Transportation & Logistics (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.4%), YTL Power (+0.3%) and Petronas Dagangan (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 654 to 552, and 517 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday, supported by renewed strength in technology and semiconductor stocks, easing oil prices and improved sentiment ahead of the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI led regional gains, rising 1.7%, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.2%), Taiwan's TAIEX (+1.1%) and China's Shanghai Composite (+1.0%), while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, chipmakers led the gains, with Samsung Electronics rising 5.0% after US semiconductor stocks rallied, while semiconductor exports surged 259% YoY to USD34.1 bn in the first 20 days of September, reinforcing expectations of strong chip demand and earnings. In China, sentiment was supported by gains in technology and healthcare stocks, while the PBOC maintained its key lending rates and investors awaited the Trump-Xi meeting. European stocks closed firmly higher on Monday, supported by lower sovereign yields and easing ongoing pressures from an adverse macroeconomic backdrop. The Euro STOXX 50 gained 1.3% to 6,318 and the STOXX Europe 600 rose 1.0% to 642. Natural gas and fuel prices pulled back following the weekend amid signs that GCC nations are chasing diplomatic ways with Iran to restart tanker flows through the Persian Gulf. The drop in yields aided the outlook of credit and supported banks, with UniCredit, Nordea, and BBVA adding between 3.2% and 2%. Lastly, a global rally for the AI infrastructure sector supported Infineon with a 4.3% jump, while ASML added 2.5%. US stocks rallied on Monday, supported by falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields, while optimism over the upcoming Trump-Xi summit further lifted sentiment. The Nasdaq CI surged 2.26%, while the S&P 500 and Dow gained 1.49% and 0.71%, respectively. Meta jumped 11.3% on optimism over its AI offering, Muse, while AMD and Intel surged 10% and 12.1%, respectively. Investors now await earnings from AutoZone and KB Home, along with speeches from Federal Reserve officials. US: Treasury Yields Edge Down 4.95% on Monday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell 4bps to 4.95% on Monday, as traders started the new week with another decline in oil prices, amid hopes that diplomatic efforts could lead to a resolution to the conflict with Iran. Oil prices have now fallen for four consecutive sessions, easing some concerns over renewed inflationary pressures (Trading Economics) US: Gold Slips on Dollar Strength Gold prices edged lower toward $4,350 on Monday, pressured by a stronger US dollar and profit-taking after last week’s rally, while investors continued to monitor developments in the Middle East. Bullion reached its highest level in more than a week on Friday as falling oil prices eased concerns over prolonged inflationary pressures. Oil prices extended their decline at the start of the week as investors looked for signs of diplomatic progress on the Iran conflict around this week’s UN meetings, although tensions remained elevated as Iran and the US exchanged fresh threats on Sunday. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Decline as Supply Concerns Ease Crude oil held below $96 per barrel on Tuesday after falling for four consecutive sessions, pressured by easing supply concerns in the Middle East and growing diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. President Donald Trump is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly in New York later today and could meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines. Trump is also expected to hold discussions with other Gulf nations and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. (Trading Economics) US: AI adoption is driving hiring, but mostly for senior roles Companies using artificial intelligence are adding more jobs than those that are not but those gains sharply favour senior employees over junior workers, according to a new study spanning 41 countries. The number of employees in senior positions rose by 6.7% over five years at companies adopting AI while junior employment declined 3% in the same period, researchers Bharat Chandar of Stanford University and Bouke Klein Teeselink of King’s College London said in a paper released on Monday. (Bloomberg) US: Fed's Kashkari says inflation is still too high in 'all aspects' of US economy Minneapolis Federal Reserve president Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices. "So even if we strip out energy, which is really volatile, and strip out food — they matter a lot — but in terms of where the economy is going, inflation is still too high," Kashkari told Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures. (Reuters) US: Housing costs rise further out of reach ahead of mid-terms Barely six weeks out from the midterm elections, housing costs that many Americans have long said are too high are looking even more out of reach. The latest blow for consumers came Thursday, when Freddie Mac reported that rates for 30-year mortgages climbed to 6.95%, the highest since January 2025, when President Donald Trump returned to office. That report emerged after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, crushing any hopes that borrowing costs will come down soon. (Bloomberg) US: New data centres worth US$68 billion disrupted in US, data show Opposition to data centres continues to mount in the US. That is according to research group Data Center Watch, which said some 45 data centre projects worth US$68 billion (RM277.28 billion) were blocked or delayed by local pushback between April and June this year. Communities across the country are now pushing through moratoriums on new construction, often before developers can apply for permissions. (Bloomberg) US: EM investors are favouring local bonds as dollar debt lags Emerging-market investors are for now sticking with local-currency sovereign debt as surging Treasury yields dim the appeal of dollardenominated developing-nation bonds. Behind the strategy are attractive valuations and the potential to profit from carry trades, where investors borrow in low-yielding currencies to invest in higher-yielding assets. (Bloomberg) US: ECB launches key link between blockchain and euro payment system The European Central Bank on Monday began letting banks settle tokenised wholesale transactions in central-bank money while continuing efforts to develop a digital euro for consumers by the end of the decade. The so-called Pontes project links blockchain markets with the euro area’s existing payment systems. It will eventually be replaced by a longer-term solution known as Appia, for which a blueprint should be ready in 2028. (Bloomberg) CN: Yuan hits fresh multi-year peak as China's central bank eases curb ahead of Trump-Xi summit China's yuan strengthened to more than a 3-1/2-year high against the US dollar on Monday as the central bank softened its curb on currency appreciation ahead of the meeting this week between the leaders of China and the US.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng concluded talks in New York on Sunday, laying the groundwork for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to consider at their summit from Sept 23-25. (Reuters) SK: Early exports maintain strong momentum on chip boom South Korea’s exports continued to grow at a solid pace in early September as global demand for artificial-intelligence supported semiconductor shipments and the broader trade-dependent economy. Exports adjusted for working-day differences rose 89.8% from a year earlier in the first 20 days of September, according to customs office data released Monday. That compared with an initially reported 61.5% increase during the same period in August. (Bloomberg) MY: Nearly two-thirds of Malaysians make RM2,200 or less a month in 2025 - official data Nearly two-thirds of Malaysia’s wage earners were in semi- and low-skilled jobs in 2025, with median monthly wages of RM2,223 or less, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). Semi-skilled workers, who accounted for 55.6% of wage earners, had a median monthly wage of RM2,223, while low-skilled workers, who make up 7.8% of wage earners, earned RM1,758. Skilled workers, by comparison, earned a median RM5,057. Skilled workers make up 36.6% of total wage recipients. (The Edge) MY: Malaysians' average monthly salary up 4% to RM3,803 in 2025 - DOSM The average monthly salary and wage of Malaysians increased by 4.1% to RM3,803 in 2025, compared with RM3,652 the previous year, according to the Salaries and Wages Survey Report 2025 published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) on Monday. At the same time, the median monthly salary and wage increased by 5.3 % to RM2,940 from RM2,793 in 2024. (Berrnama) MY: REIT managers call for return of withholding tax relief in Budget 2027 The Malaysian REIT Managers Association (MRMA) hopes the withholding tax break on real estate investment trusts (REITs) dividends will be restored in Budget 2027. AmFIRST Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) manager and chief executive officer Chong Hong Chuon told reporters after its annual general meeting and extraordinary general meeting that the association had submitted its requests to the government, including a review of the tax treatment for REIT distributions. (Berrnama) AAGB: Malaysia wins best low-cost airline award for 17th year as it renews operating certificate AirAsia Malaysia, the carrier operated by AirAsia Group Bhd, was recognised as the World’s Best Low-Cost Airline for the 17th consecutive year at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards in London last Friday.The latest win comes as the airline marks 25 years of operations. (The Edge) INSPACE: Bags RM35 mil subcontract for renovation works Interior fit-out firm Inspace Creation Bhd has won a subcontract of RM34.75 million to undertake renovation works on commercial properties. In a Bursa Malaysia filing on Monday, the group stated that its indirectly wholly owned subsidiary, IDPM Builder Sdn Bhd, had accepted a letter of award for the project from an undisclosed customer on Monday. The company said it could not disclose the identity of the main contractor as well as the location of the project and specific details of the subcontract due to confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Hits four-year high after slew of good news Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd, hit a four-year high on Monday in a sudden spike in its share price, which came amid a slew of positive developments, including the renewal of a 10-year product supply deal with Shell Malaysia two weeks ago. The spike comes as brent crude futures fell to a week’s low of US$101.7 (RM415.06) a barrel. (The Edge) PWRWELL: Secures RM190m orders to supply low voltage switchgear for data centre in Johor Powerwell Holdings Bhd said on Monday it has secured two contracts worth RM190.42 million for the supply of low-voltage switchgear and related equipment for a data centre project in Johor. The electrical equipment manufacturer said its wholly owned unit, Powerwell International Sdn Bhd, will be supplying the equipment to a multinational technology corporation specialising in data centres. (The Edge) DIALOG: Gets PETRONAS approval for US$81m RAJA Cluster development plan Dialog Group Bhd said its RAJA Cluster small field asset production sharing contract (PSC) has received approval from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) for an US$81 million (RM330.29 million) field development and abandonment plan. In a bourse filing on Monday, Dialog said the final investment decision for the plan was approved by PETRONAS through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM). (The Edge) EFORCE: Proposes RM11 mil private placement to fund working capital as TS Wong hit by selldowns Excel Force MSC Bhd, one of the companies linked to businessman Wong Thean Soon, has proposed a private placement to raise up to RM10.98 million for working capital and free up funds for a software project. The financial technology solutions provider plans to issue up to 60.99 million new shares, representing 10% of its existing issued share capital, to third-party investors to be identified later, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia on Monday. (The Edge) WINSTAR: Plans RM300 million sukuk for investments, land acquisition, refinancing Winstar Capital Bhd proposes to issue a RM300 million sukuk to finance investments and land acquisition, as well as to refinance existing loans. The group, which lodged the sukuk murabahah programme with the Securities Commission Malaysia on Monday, said proceeds will also be used to defray issuance expenses and for working capital. (The Edge) SPSETIA: Launches 100-acre Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines S P Setia Bhd officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines in Kepala Batas, Penang — marking a significant milestone in the group's placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. According to a press statement on Sept 21, the launch was graced by Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, alongside state representatives, government agencies, strategic partners, invited guests, residents and members of the public. (The Edge) KGB: To collaborate with Tata Group's unit on Gujarat semiconductor fabrication facility Kelington Group Bhd has entered into a collaboration with electronics and semiconductor manufacturer Tata Electronics to advance the development of the latter’s semiconductor fabrication facility (Fab) in Dholera, Gujarat. Kelington said under the agreement dated Sept 18, the group will support the Tata Group’s unit in infrastructure and system deployment for the facility. (The Edge) PEKAT: Unit to lease 470 acres in Sungai Petani for 24 years for renewable energy activities Pekat Group Bhd said on Monday that it will lease about 470 acres of land in Sungai Petani, Kedah for renewable energy activities, including the development of solar photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage systems. In a bourse filing, the engineering services firm said its wholly owned unit Pekat Teknologi Sdn Bhd had entered into a conditional lease agreement with an unnamed company to lease the land. The company cited a confidentiality obligation for its reason to not name the lessor. (The Edge) GAMUDA: JV secures RM1.8 bil Western Sydney road upgrade contract Gamuda Bhd and Australian construction group BMD Constructions Pty Ltd have secured a A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) contract to upgrade two roads in Western Sydney. Transport for New South Wales awarded the Elizabeth Drive Upgrade-Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 project to the Gamuda-BMD Joint Venture (GBJV), which is equally owned by both parties, Gamuda said in a bourse filing on Monday. Gamuda’s 50% share of the contract is expected to generate A$312 million, or about RM908 million, in revenue. The project commenced on Monday and is targeted for completion in 2030. (The Edge) CTOS: Appoints Najib's daughter Putri Norlisa as independent director Putri Norlisa Najib, the eldest daughter of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, has joined CTOS Digital Bhd as an independent non-executive director. The 45-year-old lawyer's board appointment will take effect on Sept 25, according to a bourse filing by CTOS. She is one of three children from Najib's first marriage to Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar. Putri Norlisa is currently the joint managing partner of Adnan Sundra & Low, a position she has held since 2023. (The Edge) SSB8: Unit wins RM40 mil electrical works job for Nilai data centre Southern Score Builders Bhd has won a RM40 million subcontract for electrical works at a data centre project in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan. According to a bourse filing, Southern Score Builders said the letter of award was given to its 51%-owned subsidiary SJEE Engineering Sdn Bhd from an unnamed local construction company on Monday. SJEE will be responsible for the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of electrical works, as well as maintenance and warranty services. (The Edge) STRAITS: Proposes capital reduction to wipe out RM90 million in losses Straits Energy Resources Bhd has proposed a share capital reduction to eliminate RM90 million in accumulated losses. Based on the latest unaudited results, the proposed share capital reduction would eliminate the group's RM39.17 million accumulated losses as of June 30, 2026 – resulting in retained earnings of RM50.83 million, before taking into account the estimated RM165,000 expenses related to the exercise as well as the foreign currency translation reserve of RM4.05 million, the group said in a bourse filing on Monday (Sept 21).
