title: 'Hilang Sumber Pendapatan Sejak Suami Sakit, Ibu Anak Empat Niaga Dalam Bonet Kereta Demi Sesuap Nasi
body: 'Diuji suami sakit secara tiba-tiba kerana sakit buah pinggang tahap empat dan kanser limfoma, ibu anak empat ini tetap gigih berdiri di bawah payung kecil yang dipacak di tepi bonet kereta demi mencari sesuap nasi dan selesaikan komitmen bulanan. Hilang Sumber Pendapatan Sejak Suami Sakit Kalau sebelum ini suaminya bekerja sebagai pemandu lori, sekarang hanya mampu duduk di atas kerusi dan terbaring di katil. Sesekali dia akan ulang-alik ke hospital untuk rawatan sakitnya. Dari beratnya 78kg, susut kepada 54kg disebabkan hilang selera makan. Beban mencari rezeki dan mengurus rumah tangga kini tergalas di atas bahu Puan Norin Sah binti Md Rejab selepas suaminya, Shaiful Bahari bin Muhamad Saad, 50, hanya terlantar di atas katil sejak disahkan menghidap penyakit kanser limfoma sejak bulan Januari tahun 2025. Ibu Anak Empat Niaga Dalam Bonet Kereta Demi Sesuap Nasi Setiap kali pelajar sekolah keluar dari pintu pagar, setiap kali itu lah wajah wanita berusia 44 tahun ini akan tersenyum dek kerana akan ada rezekinya masuk apabila jualan aiskrim Malaysia dan buah potongnya dibeli. Nampak kecil tetapi nilainya cukup besar bagi ibu yang gigih mencari rezeki demi anak-anak tersayang. Ibu kepada empat anak itu berkata, sejak suaminya disahkan menghidap kanser, kehidupan keluarganya berubah apabila suaminya tidak lagi dapat bekerja seperti sebelum ini. Tidak berharap lebih, tetapi cukuplah jika dapat bantu selesaikan apa yang patut dan suapkan anak-anak dengan rezeki yang halal. “Saya sendiri buntu memikirkan di mana hendak mencari duit selepas ini kerana perlu membuat bayaran macam-macam. Jual Makanan dalam bonet kereta tidak lah dapat banyak mana. tapi alhamdulillah, lepas lah buat beli lauk” katanya. Apabila keluar berniaga, Puan Norin atau lebih mesra dipanggil Kak Sya terpaksa tinggal suaminya di rumah sekejap. Dari segi sumbangan, ada dapat sedikit daripada kejiranan dan kebajikan sekitar taman. Orang ramai yang berhasrat membantu meringankan beban Kak Sya, boleh terus memberikan sumbangan menerusi nombor akaun ini: Maybank: 152116003190 Nama: Norin Sah binti Md Rejab Nilainya tak banyak tak mengapa, yang penting ikhlas untuk meringankan beban ibu ini. Semoga dengan sedikit pemberian kita hari ini dapat membuatkan wajah seseorang yang diuji kembali tersenyum dan rasa masih ada harapan untuk melangkah ke depan.

title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460. This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee

title: '国行:大马金融风险可控 需警惕地缘政治冲击 - 财经 - 焦点财经
body: '国行:大马金融风险可控 需警惕地缘政治冲击 （吉隆坡5日讯）中东地缘政治冲突成全球经济及金融市场主要下行风险“源头”，但国家银行指出，这对国内金融市场潜在带来的冲击仍处可管理水平，且整体金融体系直接受中东冲突的影响有限。  国行今日在主题为“国际油价以外：从地缘政治冲突到金融稳定风险”的10月观察报告披露，尽管国内金融体系展现韧性，但并无法完全免疫于未来冲击。 “因此，国行将保持警惕，持续开展监测工作，重点关注企业流动性、脆弱企业与家庭的还款趋势、银行融资状况，以及冲击经金融市场被放大的可能性。” 银行股表现不俗 马股金融服务指数今日走稳，闭市时起0.52%收在19140.14点。在32只银行股中，半数走高，以丰隆银行（HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组）表现最为亮眼，冲高24仙至22令吉88仙，是场内第11大上升股。 其他表现不俗还有大马银行（AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组），闭市报6令吉50仙，攀高11仙。至于联昌集团（CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组）和大众银行（PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组）则分别走高8仙与5仙，收在7令吉73仙及4令吉71仙。 贵为马股最大市值的马来亚银行（MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组）今日在9令吉98仙至10令吉10仙区间拉扯，最终滑落2仙收在10令吉。 报告点出，金融稳定风险虽仍可控，但在市场不确定性持续的情况下，还需保持警惕；若中东冲突进一步恶化或更持久，恐将对原产品带来更大的价格冲击、持续扰乱供应链，及拖累全球经济增长前景。 “随着投资者重新评估地缘政治发展、原产品价格前景以及主要经济体利率走向，全球金融市场料续高度波动。尽管如此，迄今为止的种种数据显示，这些对国内金融稳定风险还是处于可管理水平。” 国行表示，金融压力目前主要集中在特定领域及特定借贷人群体，整体信贷素质还稳健，且融资持续流向实体经济，而金融机构也维持强劲资本、流动性及拨备缓冲。 年初宏观压力测试仍可参考 报告说明，国行年初进行的宏观压力测试仍具参考意义，因有关情境已涵盖地缘政治演变所引起的全球风险规避情绪，以及供应链中断和大宗商品价格上涨所带来的通胀压力。 “而若冲突持续时间拉长或进一步恶化的潜在影响，也在上述压力测试的结果范围内，即使面对更为不利的经济环境，金融体系依然有韧性。” 国行指出，目前国内金融体系的贷款偿表现仍稳定，而压力主要集中在特定商业领域，银行的融资成本虽面临一些上行压力，但流动性状况仍获支撑。 “银行、保险公司及伊斯兰保险业者继续维持充足财务缓冲，确保金融中介活动不受干扰，另国内金融市场深度与多元化的投资者基础，也有助限制外部市场波动的传导；主要传导渠道是通过实体经济和全球金融市场，而非是信贷或融资风险敞口传导。” 此外，报告认为，避险情绪升温也可能促使投资者重新调整组合，加剧资本流动波动，影响资产估值、债券回酬率、汇率及市场流动性。综合来看，这些影响可能导致信贷及融资收紧。 “这对金融机构的相关影响，最终或体现在更高信贷及理赔成本、估值损失、融资及流动性压力，以及获利和资本能力减弱。” 国行指出，地缘政治冲突引起的冲击并非孤立发生，而是与其他全球经济及金融发展相互叠加，至于对国内金融稳定的影响，取决于这些综合冲击与现有金融脆弱性的相互作用。 “目前的迹象显示，金融压力进一步放大的风险仍有限，金融体系的高度韧性足以吸纳相关冲击带来的影响。整体商业状况持稳，主要是国内需求持续、电子电器产品出口强劲，以及投资活动持续。” 中小企普遍面对挑战 不过，国行在与企业交流的过程发现，部分企业正面对投入及物流成本上升、付款延迟，以及现金周转周期拉长等问题。 “这些挑战在中小型企业更普遍，因通常赚幅较薄、流动性缓冲较小，在多元化供应商或吸收成本上涨方面的空间也较有限。这情况在批发及零售贸易、建筑业，以及部分制造领域尤其明显。” 报告披露，企业也已采取相应措施缓和营运压力，包括改善成本效率、多元化供应商及采购渠道、调整生产与库存计划，和加强现金流管理。 “截至目前，这些调整措施有助控制企业财务状况所受到的影响，整体企业贷款素质仍稳健。截至今年6月，企业总减值贷款率为2.8%，而被归类为信用风险增加的第二阶段贷款占比，仍低于近期平均水平。” 不过，国行提醒，部分中小企业已出现偿债压力，包括交通物流、批发及零售贸易，以及初级制造领域。 “这些情况说明，部分持续面对流动性压力的企业，潜在的信贷风险可能正在累积，因此持续从借款人及行业层面进行监测，还是相当重要。” 金融市场压力指数升 另一方面，国行点出，地缘政治紧张情绪升温，加上市场对美国货币政策预期的变化，导致全球风险情绪转变，并持续加剧金融市场波动，这些发展促使包括我国在内的新兴市场外国投资者，重新调整组合配置。 “与此同时，马股与指数相关的再平衡操作（将综指成分股扩大至50只），也影响外国投资者的持仓情况。随着外部环境波动加剧，金融市场压力指数平均为9%，比2021至2025年平均7.4%的水平高。” 美国与伊朗今年4月达成2周停火协议前，这个压力指数曾从14.2%的高峰回落，但因地缘政治持续不确定性，以及近期先进经济体债券回酬率走高夹击，这压力指数仍维持在较高水平。 尽管如此，国行相信，国内金融市场仍有能力吸收这些外部冲击，并保持有序运作。 “境内外汇市场维持稳健，平均每日成交额达219亿美元（约894亿令吉）。马币兑美元汇率今年以来按年贬值0.43%，纵然美元整体走势波动，但我国经济基本面稳定持续助力马币走稳。” 而报告也点出，大马政府债券回酬率紧随全球债券回酬率走高，尽管外国投资者持续调整投资组合，但今年来在我国持有的政府债券仍增加81亿令吉。 “大马政府债券与美国国债之间的回酬率落差续扩大，加上届满的政府债券规模较大，可能增加投资组合资金流动对外部环境变化的敏感度，但深厚的金融市场和多元化投资者基础，加上国内金融机构韧性，将继续支撑市场有序运作。” 国行重申，国内银行领域仍有余力可吸收不利经济及金融环境所带来的影响，银行体系总资本适足率为风险加权资产的17.9%，远高于监管要求。 信贷风险仍受控 “而强劲的盈利能力进一步增强银行体系的韧性，股本回酬和资产回酬率分别为11.5%和1.3%。另外信贷风险仍受控，截至今年6月的整体贷款减值率维持在1.4%，而第二阶段贷款占比则今年3月的6.1%降至5.9%。” 报告指出，银行领域也继续维持审慎拨备水平，贷款损失覆盖率（包括监管储备）为124.6%，流动性及融资状况同样保持稳健。银行体系整体流动性覆盖率和净稳定资金比率分别为149.6%和114.7%，均高于监管最低要求。 存款竞争加剧 “部分融资工具的融资成本逐步上升，归咎于银行争取存款的竞争加剧，对融资成本造成一定的上行压力，但涨幅仍在可控范围内。无论如何，这些变化尚未演变成更广泛的融资压力，也没有限制银行支持信贷中介活动的能力。”  热门新闻 百格视频

entities.text: 因此，国行将保持警惕，持续开展监测工作，重点关注企业流动性、脆弱企业与家庭的还款趋势、银行融资状况，以及冲击经金融市场被放大的可能性
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: 银行股表现不俗 马股金融服务指数今日走稳，闭市时起0.52%收在19140.14点。在32只银行股中，半数走高，以丰隆银行（HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组）表现最为亮眼，冲高24仙至22令吉88仙，是场内第11大上升股
entities.label: PERSON

entities.text: 其他表现不俗还有大马银行（AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组），闭市报6令吉50仙，攀高11仙。至于联昌集团（CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组）和大众银行（PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组）则分别走高8仙与5仙，收在7令吉73仙及4令吉71仙
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: 国行表示，金融压力目前主要集中在特定领域及特定借贷人群体，整体信贷素质还稳健，且融资持续流向实体经济，而金融机构也维持强劲资本、流动性及拨备缓冲
entities.label: GPE

entities.text: 年初宏观压力测试仍可参考 报告说明，国行年初进行的宏观压力测试仍具参考意义，因有关情境已涵盖地缘政治演变所引起的全球风险规避情绪，以及供应链中断和大宗商品价格上涨所带来的通胀压力
entities.label: PERSON

entities.text: 国行指出，目前国内金融体系的贷款偿表现仍稳定，而压力主要集中在特定商业领域，银行的融资成本虽面临一些上行压力，但流动性状况仍获支撑
entities.label: PERSON

entities.text: 此外，报告认为，避险情绪升温也可能促使投资者重新调整组合，加剧资本流动波动，影响资产估值、债券回酬率、汇率及市场流动性。综合来看，这些影响可能导致信贷及融资收紧
entities.label: PERSON

entities.text: 国行指出，地缘政治冲突引起的冲击并非孤立发生，而是与其他全球经济及金融发展相互叠加，至于对国内金融稳定的影响，取决于这些综合冲击与现有金融脆弱性的相互作用
entities.label: PERSON

entities.text: 目前的迹象显示，金融压力进一步放大的风险仍有限，金融体系的高度韧性足以吸纳相关冲击带来的影响。整体商业状况持稳，主要是国内需求持续、电子电器产品出口强劲，以及投资活动持续
entities.label: DATE

entities.text: 不过，国行提醒，部分中小企业已出现偿债压力，包括交通物流、批发及零售贸易，以及初级制造领域
entities.label: PERSON

title: 'Doktor rugi RM300,000 terpedaya pelaburan Kad Prihatin Siswa
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR - Seorang doktor swasta berusia 38 tahun kerugian RM300,000 selepas terpedaya dengan tawaran pelaburan Projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang didakwa membabitkan sebuah syarikat, pada awal 2023.  Ketua Polis Daerah Ampang Jaya, Asisten Komisioner Khairul Anuar Khalid berkata, mangsa diperdaya suspek yang mendakwa projek berkenaan membabitkan 20 universiti dengan kira-kira 620,000 pelajar.  Katanya, suspek turut menjanjikan pulangan keuntungan kepada mangsa sebelum mangsa membuat lima transaksi berjumlah RM300,000 ke akaun Maybank milik suspek.  “Satu perjanjian pelaburan turut ditandatangani dengan menjanjikan keuntungan 10 peratus sebulan selama 12 bulan serta pemulangan modal selepas tamat tempoh perjanjian.  “Mangsa juga didaftarkan sebagai pemegang 10 peratus saham syarikat tersebut,” katanya menerusi kenyataan hari ini.  Bagaimanapun, Khairul Anuar berkata, mangsa yang merupakan wanita tidak pernah menerima keuntungan dan dividen seperti yang dijanjikan.  “Suspek turut gagal memberikan penyelesaian walaupun telah beberapa kali diminta penjelasan. Mangsa kemudiannya membuat laporan polis untuk tindakan lanjut,” katanya.  Beliau berkata, kes kini disiasat mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan kerana menipu.  Sehubungan itu, beliau menasihatkan orang ramai supaya tidak mudah terpedaya dengan tawaran pelaburan yang menjanjikan pulangan tinggi.  “Orang ramai disaran membuat semakan terlebih dahulu melalui portal rasmi Semak Mule PDRM serta mendapatkan maklumat berkaitan status dan kesahihan tawaran pelaburan melalui Suruhanjaya Sekuriti Malaysia (SC) dan Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) sebelum membuat sebarang transaksi,” katanya. - MalaysiaGazette

title: 'Doktor diperdaya bapa bekas penyanyi, polis siasat penipuan pelaburan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa
body: 'Ampang Jaya: Polis sudah membuka kertas siasatan membabitkan penipuan pelaburan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang dikaitkan dengan sebuah syarikat milik seorang lelaki yang juga bapa kepada bekas penyanyi. Ketua Polis Daerah Ampang Jaya, Asisten Komisioner Khairul Anuar Khalid berkata, mangsa, doktor swasta berusia 38 tahun pada awal 2023 bersama suaminya berurusan dengan suspek berkaitan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang dikaitkan dengan sebuah syarikat secara bersemuka dan melalui WhatsApp. Menurutnya, suspek memperkenalkan projek terbabit sebagai pelaburan yang membabitkan 20 buah universiti dan kira-kira 620,000 pelajar serta menjanjikan pulangan keuntungan kepada pelabur. "Mangsa membuat lima kali transaksi pembayaran dengan jumlah keseluruhan sebanyak RM300,000 ke atas nombor akaun Maybank milik suspek sepanjang 2023. "Selepas daripada itu, satu perjanjian pelaburan ditandatangani yang menyatakan pelaburan sebanyak RM300,000 dengan keuntungan sebanyak 10 peratus sebulan selama 12 bulan dan modal akan dipulangkan pada tamat tempoh perjanjian," katanya dalam kenyataan hari ini. Beliau berkata, mangsa kemudiannya didaftarkan sebagai pemegang 10 peratus saham syarikat terbabit. "Bagaimanapun, keuntungan dan dividen yang dijanjikan tidak pernah diterima. Mangsa dan suami beberapa kali meminta penjelasan, pembayaran dividen serta salinan perjanjian yang dimatikan setem, namun suspek memberikan pelbagai alasan dan gagal memberikan penyelesaian. "Siasatan dijalankan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan dan tiada tangkapan setakat ini," katanya. Harian Metro hari ini melaporkan lelaki itu meyakinkan pelabur bahawa projek Kad Prihatin Siswa membabitkan 20 universiti mampu menjana pulangan lumayan dan kononnya ingin membantu lebih ramai orang Melayu kaya sepertinya. Itu taktik seorang lelaki bergelar Datuk yang juga bapa kepada bekas penyanyi memperdayakan pasangan doktor sehingga menyebabkan kerugian RM300,000 selepas melabur sejak 2023. Malah, dia turut mendakwa berkawan dengan pegawai tertinggi kerajaan dan kononnya minit mesyuarat projek ini juga sudah dihantar ke kerajaan dengan 620,000 pelajar akan menikmati kad terbabit hasil kerjasama dengan syarikat telekomunikasi terkenal.

title: 'Restock Sambal Nyet Bilis, Khairul Aming Sekali Lagi Capai ‘Sales’ RM2 Juta - Gempak

title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah to hold wedding receptions in Muar & Kota Kinabalu, public invited to 'Kenduri Rakyat'
body: 'Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and Malaysian singer-actress Bella Astillah, who are set to marry on Oct 10, will celebrate their special occasion with the public through two receptions themed “Kenduri Rakyat”.  The couple, who got engaged on March 28, will first exchange vows at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur.  The celebrations will then continue in Muar, Johor, on Oct 25, before the couple heads to Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on Oct 31.  At a press conference in Kuala Lumpur today (Oct 2), Syed Saddiq said preparations for the receptions had been challenging, as the events were organised within a span of two months.  Much of the difficulty came from finding enough vendors and a suitable venue within the limited timeframe.  “We are expecting around 20,000 to 30,000 guests. We will do our best to accommodate everyone,” the former youth and sports minister said. title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah anjur 'Kenduri Rakyat' rai perkahwinan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bakal mempelai, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan tunangnya, Bella Astillah menjemput orang ramai menghadiri majlis 'Kenduri Rakyat' di Muar, Johor dan Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, selepas mereka diijabkabulkan di sini, pada 10 Oktober ini. 'Kenduri Rakyat' meraikan perkahwinan Syed Saddiq dan Bella akan diadakan di Muar, Johor pada 25 Oktober, diikuti Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, pada 31 Oktober. Syed Saddiq yang juga Ahli Parlimen Muar berkata, kedua-dua majlis resepsi dirancang dalam tempoh kurang dua bulan dan mereka berdepan kekangan masa serta kesukaran mendapatkan lokasi majlis perkahwinan. "Majlis kahwin kami nanti bertemakan rewang. Kalau sebelum ini, sambutan Hari Raya yang saya anjurkan di Muar sudah mencecah 10,000 orang, jadi, kita jangka untuk kenduri kami lebih ramai yang akan datang. "Jadi, majlis itu nanti berkonsepkan 'siapa cepat dia dapat' (nikmati juadah). Jika makanan habis sekalipun, kami akan berada di sana untuk bersama dengan tetamu," katanya pada majlis Walimatulurus Bella Astillajh & Syed Saddiq di sini, hari ini. Difahamkan, sebanyak 10,000 cenderahati istimewa disediakan untuk tetamu. Sebelum ini, Syed Saddiq dan Bella dilapor mengesahkan bakal disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada 10 Oktober ini. Syed Saddiq dan Bella dilapor mula berkenalan dengan lebih rapat pada 2025 sebelum mengikat tali pertunangan pada 28 Mac lalu.

title: 'Nanta titip pesanan buat Syed Saddiq, Bella-‘Perkahwinan umpama jalan raya’
body: 'MENTERI Kerja Raya Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi berkongsikan pertemuannya dengan bakal pengantin Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan selebriti Bella Astillah.  Namun, apa yang lebih menarik nasihat dititipkan Nanta terhadap pasangan dua sejoli itu yang sedang menghitung hari untuk bergelar raja sehari.  Pesanan Nanta kepada pasangan berkenaan agak menarik apabila menyifatkan perkahwinan “seumpama jalan raya”.  “Bila berjumpa orang muda yang bakal melangkah ke alam perkahwinan, sempatlah saya kongsi sedikit pesanan.  “Saya kata, perkahwinan ni umpama jalan raya — mesti dua hala, tak boleh sehala. Kena saling memberi, saling menerima dan sama-sama bertolak ansur.  “Dalam rumah tangga, bukan soal siapa betul atau siapa menang. Yang penting, dua-dua kena tahu bila nak jalan, bila nak berhenti, dan kadang-kadang bila kena bagi laluan,” katanya dalam hantaran di Facebooknya.  Nanta turut mendoakan agar segala urusan Syed Saddiq dan Bella dipermudahkan dan semoga perjalanan yang bakal ditempuh bersama nanti sentiasa diberkati dan dipenuhi kebahagiaan.  Syed Saddiq dan Bella dijadualkan akan melangsungkan akad nikah pada 10 Oktober ini di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur.- MalaysiaPost

title: 'Opinion: When audit opinions meet uncertain numbers
body: 'Two lawsuits filed within days of each other in late July and early August have renewed a question that matters to every investor. When financial statements rest on estimates that could go either way, what does a “clean” audit opinion actually guarantee? The liquidators of Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd are seeking at least RM1.56 billion from KPMG, alleging that unqualified opinions between FY2016 and FY2019 failed to detect revenue overstatements of up to 87%. The suit claims the misstatements would have been uncovered earlier, before the group paid RM1.795 billion in dividends, which the claim links to the alleged audit failures. Around the same time, the Sabah government, together with other plaintiffs, sued Ernst & Young for RM2.4 billion over its audits of Sabah Development Bank, alleging that EY issued unqualified opinions for years even though, according to the claim, 85.94% of the bank’s loan portfolio had been recorded as non-performing loans by FY2018. Both claims remain before the courts, and the allegations have not been tested at trial. The cases will turn on negligence and evidence. But they expose a deeper structural tension that the courts cannot resolve. There is a gap between what an audit opinion actually asserts and what investors assume it guarantees. The lawsuits concern alleged audit failures. The broader issue, however, exists even where there is no allegation of failure. To see that tension clearly, it helps to separate alleged audit failure from the routine judgements in every set of audited accounts. Serba Dinamik and Sabah Development Bank are outlier cases. The structural issue is visible in ordinary audits of Malaysia’s largest companies, whose auditors have not been accused of anything. Maybank’s FY2025 audited accounts provide one illustration. The auditors identified expected credit losses on loans, advances and financing as a Key Audit Matter (KAM). These assets represent 64.3% of the group’s total assets. The auditors stated that measuring expected credit losses (ECL) “requires the application of significant judgement and increased complexity”, involving forward looking factors, probability weighted scenarios and management overlays. They tested models, challenged assumptions and engaged credit modelling specialists. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s FY2025 statements offer another. Post employment benefit liabilities of RM13.3 billion at group level were valued using actuarial assumptions on salary increases, medical cost inflation and discount rates. The auditors “focused on this area because of the significant estimates made by management”, checked assumptions against historical data and compared discount rates to market yields with valuation experts. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. These are not presented as cases of audit failure. The system is working as designed. Yet TNB reports that a one percentage point movement in the discount rate can change its defined benefit obligation by more than RM1 billion. Maybank’s KAM similarly describes extensive audit procedures without showing investors the range of possible outcomes. The KAM explains the judgement, but not how sensitive the number may be. International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 701 requires auditors to communicate KAMs and allow them to highlight matters requiring significant auditor attention, while the opinion remains on the financial statements as a whole. But the framework is binary while uncertainty is not. Two competent valuers may reach different estimates, and a figure can be reasonable without being the only supportable answer. KAMs can therefore become lists of procedures rather than explanations of risk. Estimation uncertainty exists on a continuum while audit reporting remains categorical. The question is not whether KAMs should exist, but whether they tell investors enough about how uncertain the most consequential numbers really are. Malaysia’s Audit Oversight Board has identified “failure to sufficiently review significant risk areas and significant judgements” as a recurring enforcement concern. The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) highlighted in its November 2025 statement the importance of high-quality valuation practices, appropriate use of valuation experts and rigorous audit assessment. The International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR) has likewise identified accounting estimates, including fair value measurement, as an area where audit regulators have consistently found deficiencies. When auditors use KAMs to flag a valuation without qualifying the opinion, they are telling investors that the matter involved significant judgement but that the financial statements nevertheless met the requirements for an unmodified opinion. That may be technically correct for Maybank and TNB. But the Serba Dinamik case illustrates how insufficient that signal can be for investors. The concern is not simply whether auditors get the judgement wrong. Even a sound audit can leave investors unable to see how fragile a reasonable estimate may be. That is the gap the current reporting model should address. Four reforms would help. First, require sensitivity disclosure in the KAM. Auditors should disclose the reasonable range of outcomes and its impact on the financial statements. TNB’s statements already include sensitivity analysis on discount rate assumptions. This information should be connected directly to the KAM, rather than leaving investors to piece the implications together from different sections of the annual report. Second, consider graduated reporting for significant estimation uncertainty. Such reporting could signal that an estimate falls within an acceptable range but remains highly sensitive, without implying that there is a material misstatement. The existing Emphasis of Matter framework under ISA 706 could provide a starting point. Third, require independent valuation review for specified material Level 3 assets. A second valuation would provide an additional check on management bias. The auditor could assess the divergence as evidence and consider the additional data point when applying professional scepticism. Fourth, strengthen audit committee disclosure. Audit committees should disclose how they challenged management’s fair value assumptions. If the committee accepted management’s numbers without meaningful scrutiny, that should be visible to shareholders. None of these solutions are radical. Each builds on existing frameworks, including Malaysian Financial Reporting Standard 13 (MFRS 13), ISA 701, ISA 540 and Malaysia’s corporate governance code. They require recognition that the current approach to fair value auditing, while technically sound, is insufficiently transparent for the risks involved. Judgement is unavoidable. Opacity is not. A KAM should do more than say, “we looked at this”. It should help investors understand what drove the estimate, how sensitive it is and what could change the auditor’s assessment. A “clean” audit opinion was never meant to guarantee that every number is right. But as financial statements rely increasingly on complex estimates, audit reporting should show more clearly how uncertain the most consequential numbers are. Hijat A Jabbar and Siti Zabedah Saidin are professors of accounting at Universiti Utara Malaysia.

body: '（巴生1日讯）班达马兰华小B校将于10月17日（星期六）晚上7时正，在该校冷气大礼堂举办“文艺·相聚·闪耀班B”文艺晚宴，吁请各界慷慨解囊共募学校发展经费。 大会主席兼董事会总务范忠星在新闻发布会指出，该校家教协会举办此项文艺晚宴是为了发扬中华文化、丰富校园人文气息，并为学生打造一个展现才华的广阔舞台。 他说，此项盛会不仅是孩子们展现艺术潜能的重要时刻，更是凝聚家长及各界热心华教力量、共谋学校未来发展的重要契机。 “本次晚宴的核心目的旨在筹募发展经费，其重点用途包括支持家教协会的日常运作、全力推动校内才艺与文艺发展、提升与翻修陈旧的校园设施，以及全面增设智慧黑板。” 他期望通过这一系列的软硬件升级，为莘莘学子营造一个更优质、更具科技感与人文气息的学习与成长环境。 筹委会主席兼家教协会主席林珮雯则呼吁社会贤达、家长及热心华教人士踊跃支持，共襄盛举。 她强调，班B华小一直以来获得各界热心华教人士与家长的鼎力支持。面对庞大的校园建设与活动发展开支，单凭学校现有资源难以尽善尽美，因此恳切期盼广大热心家长及社会贤达能慷慨解囊。 她说，筹委会特设多项赞助方案： 鸣锣贵宾：捐献1万2000令吉或以上（受邀为大会鸣锣贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席1桌）。 击鼓贵宾：捐献6000令吉 或以上（受邀为大会击鼓贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席名誉券5张）。 亮灯贵宾：捐献3000令吉 或以上（受邀为大会亮灯贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席名誉券2张）。 赞助贵宾：捐献 RM1,000 或以上（受邀为大会赞助贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席名誉券2张）；捐献500令吉或以上（获赠宴席名誉券1张）。 她说，大众也可选择捐购宴席每桌1500令吉，或随缘捐献。 有意赞助或购票的善长仁翁，款项可通过现金、支票或银行转账交至各班班主任或筹委会负责人处。 银行转账详情：银行名称：MAYBANK；户头名称：PIBG SJK(C）PANDAMARAN B PEL KLANG；户头号码：5124 5512 5645；备注（Reference）：SUMBANGAN 1017（银行转账资料请附上交予班主任或筹委会负责人）；支票抬头请写明：PIBG SJK(C）PANDAMARAN B PEL KLANG 任何垂询，欢迎联络家协主席林珮雯（电话号码：012-351 5115）、校长郑长杰（电话号码：012-2878738）、票务主任张绣琴（电话号码：016-227 2232）或家协财政纪惠霞（电话号码：016-712 2816）。

Bumitama Agri's blunder on locking in its 1HFY2021 forward sales contracts at 20% to 25% lower than current prices – excluding taxes and levies – has caused analysts to downgrade the palm oil company. This is despite the Indonesia-based company's stellar results for FY2020 ended Dec 31. Bumitama had expected crude palm oil (CPO) to fall after Indonesia implemented a new tax structure. That led the company to lock in its sales contracts at a reduced price. However, CPO prices are hovering at about RM4,000 ($1,307) per metric tonne. RHB Securities has now rated the stock with a "sell" call from "buy" previously and lowered its lower target price to 45 cents from 60 cents. RHB says Bumitama would be selling CPO at close to cash-cost levels for January and February 2021 given the current tax structure in place. "This is negative, especially given our view that crude palm oil (CPO) prices will only remain elevated in 1HFY2021 before moderating in 2HFY2021," RHB says in a note dated Feb 22. The brokerage has lowered its FY2021 earnings forecast for the company by 24%. Meanwhile, Maybank Kim Eng has slashed its target price to 65 cents from 78 cents previously, albeit keeping its "buy" rating for the stock. The brokerage says the substantial forward sales at low prices are "party poopers". As part of the contract, it notes that Bumitama is expected to bear the difference between the ultimate statutory export taxes and agreed upon US$55 ($72.60) per metric tonne export tax. "This contract clause is negative on Bumitama's earnings as long as CPO spot prices are high," Maybank KE analyst Ong Chee Ting writes in a note dated Feb 22. The brokerage has reduced its FY2021 earnings per share forecast by 10%. As at 12.49 pm, Bumitama was down 1.5 cents or 2.9% at 49.5 cents with 2.3 million shares changed hands. 5 days ago After we called Bumitama and found out their Forward Sales Lost only about 30% we loaded up more Bumitama shares at S$0.46 Today plus dividend received we have made more than 400% from our BUY (SOLD DOWN VALUE) IN FEAR TIME 5 days ago Read all our history & success in Bumitama https://sgx.i3investor.com/web/stock/overview/P8Z 5 days ago TSH Resources Berhad (KLSE: TSH) experienced severe downward pressure on Friday, September 25, 2026, with its share price collapsing by 4.20% (-RM 0.06) to close at its absolute intraday low of RM 1.37. body: 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. Immediate support for the index stays at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). Meanwhile, immediate resistance is maintained at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Any weakness on Maybank shares towards the 38.2%FR (RM9.74) or the 23.6%FR (RM9.27) should encourage buying on weakness ahead of recovery upside towards the 76.4%FR (RM10.96) with next resistance coming from the 25/02/26 high (RM11.71). Sime Darby shares remain in base building mode pending recovery to the 123.6%FP (RM2.67), with a confirmed breakout to aim for the 138.2%FP (RM2.82) and 150%FP (RM2.94), while immediate chart supports are from the 30-day ma (RM2.45) and 76.4%FR (RM2.19). body: '美国就业数据前市场谨慎，周四亚洲股市淡静，马股综合指数低开，午后跌势加深，闭市重挫近21点。 截至下午闭市，综合指数跌20.81点或1.26%，至1,630.36点。 市场整体表现偏软，全场下跌股750只，上涨股342只，495只平盘，另1174只股无交易。全天成交量30.99亿股，总成交额27.29亿令吉。 30只综指成分股有·27只·下跌，仅2只微涨，另外一只平盘。吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌78仙至21.42令吉，齐力工业（PMETAL，8869，主板工业股）跌29仙至7.16令吉，国油贸易（PETDAG，5681，主板能源股）和马电讯（TM，4863，主板电讯与媒体股）各跌16仙，分别收在19.12令吉和7.85令吉。 此外，杨忠礼电力（YTLPOWR，6742，主板公用事业股）和SD牙直利（SDG，5285，主板种植股）跌各跌15仙，分别收在5.72令吉和6.05令吉，IHH医疗保健集团（IHH，5225，主板保健股）跌13仙至7.70令吉，99迷你市场集团（99SMART，5326 ，主板消费股）跌11仙至3.04令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）跌4仙至9.95令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）跌3仙4.67令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）跌10仙至7.69令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）跌3仙至7.47令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）跌30仙至22.84令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）涨1仙至6.30令吉。 热门股方面，今天首日上市的GB联合（GBBOND，0475，创业板工业股）跌4.5仙（比IPO价低18%）至20.5仙，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）涨0.5仙至16.5仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）跌1仙至27仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）跌2.5仙至18仙，迪耐（DNEX，4456，主板科技股）涨1仙至495仙 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨72仙至41.12令吉，亚逸控股（AYER，2305，主板产业股）涨20仙至7.70令吉；安联保险（ALLIANZ，1163，主板金融股）跌62仙至21.00令吉，联合种植（UTDPLT，2089，主板种植股）跌60仙至30.96令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数跌 0.14% 至 5,667.68 点，日本日经指255数起 3.30% 至 68,958.72 点，韩国首尔综合指数起 1.95% 至 6,971.35 点。香港和中国股市适逢中国国庆日假期休市。

title: 'Hap Seng Consolidated to Sell Singapore Listed Unit Hafary for S$140 Mil
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 28): Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd (KL:HAPSENG) said it plans to sell its Singapore-listed building materials unit for about S$140 million (RM447 million) following a takeover offer. 23 Capital Pte Ltd is offering cash per share of S$0.64, or RM2.04, to take private Hafary Holdings Ltd and Hap Seng Consolidated has agreed to accept the offer for its 50.82% stake, according to an exchange filing. 23 Capital is a vehicle owned by the Hafary founding family. The proposed disposal will allow Hap Seng Consolidated to realise its investment in Hafary at a premium over its initial cost of just S$0.24 per share, as well as above market and historical trading prices, the company said. If the deal goes through, Hafary will cease to be a subsidiary of Hap Seng Consolidated, preventing any consolidation of any financial results. Hap Seng Consolidated will book an estimated gross gain on disposal of about RM187.3 million from the deal expected to be completed before the year ends. While it will miss out on future earnings from Hafary, “the proposed disposal enables the group to realise its investment in cash at an attractive valuation, thereby strengthening its financial position and enhancing financial flexibility”, Hap Seng Consolidated said. Proceeds from the sale have been earmarked by Hap Seng Consolidated for partial repayment of borrowings totalling RM6.9 billion at the end of 2025. Hafary, which manufactures and trades building materials such as tiles, stone, mosaic, wood-flooring, quartz tops and sanitary ware and fittings, contributed RM48.4 million to Hap Seng Consolidated’s profit and RM19.85 million in dividends. Low Kok Ann, a Singaporean and chief executive of Hafary, controls 23 Capital with his son Low See Ching and daughter Low Bee Lan. The elder Low, also known as Eric Low, started the business from a single ceramic tile shop in 1980. Hap Seng Consolidated bought into Hafary in 2015 as a stepping stone to expand in the region. At the time of the acquisition, Hap Seng Consolidated was mainly involved in upstream segment of the building materials market while Hafary was strong downstream. Maybank Investment Bank is as principal adviser to Hap Seng Consolidated while United Overseas Bank is advising the buyer 23 Capital. title: 'Mahkamah Tinggi kekal keputusan timbang tara anugerah RM77 juta kepada SUJV
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Mahkamah Tinggi mengekalkan keputusan Tribunal Timbang Tara menganugerahkan RM77 juta kepada kontraktor utama Menara Merdeka Maybank (sebelum ini dikenali Menara Merdeka 118). Keputusan tribunal menghendaki Global Wall (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (GWM) membayar RM77,022,327.67 kepada Samsung C&T Corporation UEM Construction JV Sdn Bhd (SUJV) membabitkan pertikaian kerja fasad bagi projek mercu tanda berkenaan. Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman, Rajes Raghavuji menolak permohonan GWM mencabar keputusan itu, dengan memutuskan isu dibangkitkan sama ada secara individu atau kumulatif, gagal melepasi syarat bagi membolehkan keputusan tribunal diketepikan mengikut Akta Timbang Tara. GWM mencabar keputusan tribunal dengan alasan, antaranya melampaui bidang kuasa, pelanggaran keadilan semula jadi, kegagalan menimbangkan bukti dan hujah, tuntutan lanjutan masa dan kehilangan keuntungan. Rajes berkata, alasan itu secara intipatinya, adalah ketidaksepakatan terhadap dapatan fakta tribunal, keutamaan keterangan, dan tafsiran serta pemakaian undang-undang dan subkontrak oleh tribunal. Pertikaian timbul selepas GWM dilantik menjalankan kerja subkontrak fasad bagi pembangunan Merdeka 118. GWM menggantung kerja subkontrak pada 27 Oktober 2022, manakala SUJV kemudiannya menamatkan subkontrak berkenaan pada 18 Februari 2023. Perkara itu kemudiannya dirujuk kepada tribunal di hadapan tiga anggota terdiri daripada Ian Pennicott KC SC, Richard Wilmot-Smith KC dan David Bateson. Tribunal mendapati, kerja penggantungan kerja oleh GWM sah mengikut undang-undang, manakala penamatan subkontrak oleh SUJV adalah tidak sah. Bagaimanapun, selepas menentukan tuntutan dan tuntutan balas setiap pihak, tribunal memerintahkan GWM membayar RM77,022,327.67 kepada SUJV, faedah RM4,939,123.37 sehingga 16 Disember 2025, dengan faedah lanjut RM14,111.78 sehari dari 17 Disember 2025 sehingga pembayarannya diselesaikan. Anugerah kos berasingan memperuntukkan, 75 peratus daripada kos timbang tara memihak kepada SUJV. GWM menghujahkan, keputusan tidak munasabah kerana tribunal mendapati penamatan oleh SUJV tidak sah, namun masih memerintahkannya membayar lebih RM77 juta. Bagaimanapun, Rajes menolak hujahan itu, dengan menyatakan isu penamatan hanya satu daripada pelbagai isu dikemukakan di hadapan tribunal bagi penentuan. "Dapatan tribunal mengenai isu itu yang memihak kepada GWM tidak dengan sendirinya, menghalang SUJV daripada berjaya dalam isu bebas yang lain," katanya dalam alasan penghakiman diterbitkan Jabatan Kehakiman semalam. Rajes berkata, komponen tunggal terbesar dianugerahkan kepada SUJV ialah ganti rugi kelewatan RM33,561,503.39, yang timbul daripada kegagalan GWM menyiapkannya kerja mengikut tarikh siap yang dilanjutkan. Beliau turut mengambil perhatian, bahawa faedah RM9,691,621.22 timbul daripada pembalikan keputusan adjudikasi, manakala caj balik dan item pengambilalihan berpunca daripada dapatan ke atas tanggungjawab bagi kerja tertentu. Mahkamah juga menolak percubaan GWM untuk bersandar kepada kesan kumulatif aduannya. Rajes berkata, bilangan aduan tidak mengubah sifatnya yang, secara intipati, adalah cabaran terhadap merit keputusan tribunal. Beliau berkata, pihak-pihak sendiri memilih untuk membiarkan pertikaian mereka ditentukan panel tiga penimbang tara berpengalaman. Peguam Darshendev Singh dan Michelle Yap mewakili GWM, manakala Harold Tan, Serene Hiew dan Tan Joon Meng bertindak bagi pihak SUJV.

title: 'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai kelmarin menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja yang dirasmikan oleh Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Almarhum Sultan Iskandar Al-Haj di The Mines Resort and Golf Club. Kejohanan yang berlangsung selama tiga hari itu menyaksikan penyertaan seramai 50 pemain merangkumi kelompok profesional dan amatur termasuklah kemunculan semula juara bertahan, Liyana Durisic serta atlet Olimpik negara, Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan itu adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan selain bertindak sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Katanya, penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. “Ia adalah satu jemputan kepada generasi baharu untuk melihat golf profesional bukan sekadar sesuatu yang dimainkan di tempat lain di dunia tetapi sebagai laluan kerjaya yang boleh diceburi oleh wanita Malaysia,” katanya dalam kenyataan. title: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera maintains five sen per unit income distribution for year ended September
body: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera maintains five sen per unit income distribution for year ended September KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) has maintained its income distribution at five sen per unit for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY2026), benefitting over 82,000 unitholders. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB), together with its fund manager, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), said the final income distribution for the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, comprises 2.1 sen per unit, with an additional bonus distribution of 0.4 sen per unit declared by PHB as the fund's sponsor. "The bonus distribution will be applied to the first 1,000,000 units held by each unitholder. Including the interim income distribution of 2.5 sen per unit declared in April 2026, AHB’s total income distribution for the financial year ended FY2026 amounts to five sen per unit," the statement said. PHB said RM120.13 million will be distributed in the final round, bringing the total annual payout to RM236.41 million. PHB group managing director Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad said the full-year income distribution reflects AHB’s continued resilience and the strength of its underlying property portfolio, supported by PHB’s disciplined approach to asset and investment management. “AHB’s performance this year reaffirms our commitment to delivering competitive returns to our unitholders. At the same time, we remain focused on strengthening AHB as an investment avenue for Bumiputera investors through prudent capital management, active portfolio optimisation and strategic growth," he said. Meanwhile, PHBAM chief executive officer Zulkifli Ishak said the fund manager remains focused on managing AHB responsibly while ensuring the fund continues to serve as an accessible investment option for Bumiputera investors. PHB said income distribution will be paid in the form of AHB units, credited directly into unitholders' AHB accounts by Oct 13, 2026 and automatically reinvested, allowing unitholders to increase their unit holdings and potentially benefit from the long-term compounding effect. "Bumiputera investors who wish to subscribe to AHB may do so at a fixed price of RM1 per unit, with a minimum investment of RM100 and a maximum of RM1 million. "Subscriptions are available through the respective branches of authorised distributors nationwide, namely Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd," it said. title: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 FOR engineering outfit owner John, using artificial intelligence (AI) in his work has been a game changer. He “trains” the AI to write codes in the company’s style and now merely checks to ensure that the codes are written correctly. “I use AI to write more routine codes and it has helped me cut down coding time significantly, where a few days of work can be accomplished in 20 minutes. But I still need a few employees because engineers need to be at the physical location to make sure hardware is properly installed and conduct test runs,” he says. These days, the use of AI is prevalent in all aspects of life, in various sectors of the economy and professions, and more so among white-collar workers. Early research has shown that AI has, by some measure, improved the productivity of workers, but it still depends on the complexity of tasks and the user’s ability in AI prompting. Even so, AI is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. As a result, companies will soon be able to achieve the same outcomes with fewer workers — or, in some roles, none at all. The concern among white-collar workers about AI displacing jobs is real. Jobstreet’s Workplace Happiness Index found that while only around one-third of Malaysian workers feel “very” or “extremely” concerned about AI affecting their job security, the score is even higher among professional services workers, coming in at 47%. While there is no evidence of massive job loss as a result of AI at this juncture, recruitment agencies observe that job postings for certain roles have been declining. Jobstreet by SEEK in Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam says AI is certainly putting pressure on some forms of white-collar work, particularly roles involving repetitive, standardised or administrative tasks, many of which are being automated. Current data points, however, more towards roles being redesigned than entire professions being replaced. “The clearest early signs of pressure are in selected content and administrative roles. Job ads for positions such as content writer, copywriter, secretary and graphic designer declined between 2024 and 1H2026. We see these trends as directional indicators that automation may be changing how these roles are structured, rather than proof of one-for-one job replacement,” Lam says. This observation is consistent with a May report by the International Labour Organization (ILO), which found that studies using job postings and online labour-platform data show a significant decline in demand for skills associated with routine writing and translation, following the diffusion of generative AI (GenAI) tools, alongside increased demand for AI-related skills such as machine learning and natural language processing. PwC Malaysia managing partner Soo Hoo Khoon Yean argues that the gradual redesign of work does not necessarily imply that workers will be displaced. Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. Read also: Cover Story: AI may boost productivity, but what about workers’ share? Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. title: 'Man freed of RM108,500 cheating charge
body: 'Kota Kinabalu: A 50-year-old self-employed was freed from a charge of cheating a man involving a sum of RM108,500 over several projects in Kinabatangan and Semporna. Magistrate Wan Farrah Farriza Wan Ghazali discharged and acquitted Abdillah Hamzah without his defence being called after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him. Abdillah was accused of cheating one Chong Kong Fah by deceiving him into believing that Abdillah had managed the following projects namely, to build a concrete road to SMK Bukit Garam, Kinabatangan, to upgrade the drainage system at Bukit Permata Housing Estate, Kinabatangan, to repair the floating Jetty at Dataran Lepa-Lepa, Semporna, to upgrade the road in the Dolton Town area, Semporna and to repair houses in Semporna. The charge stated that Chong had banked-in the money into a company account under the name of Dilwani Enterprise, which he would not have done had he not been so deceived. The offence allegedly took place between June 23, 2016 and Dec 5, 2018 at the Maybank in Semporna branch. The offence under Section 420 of the Penal Code carries a jail term of up to 10 years and whipping, and liable to a fine, on conviction. The prosecution had called six witnesses during the hearing. Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Noor Hafizah Anggu standing in for DPP Arfa Anchal Khan while counsel Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip defended Abdillah. Meanwhile, a 64-year-old man pleaded guilty to causing grievous injury to another man with a machete. However, Sessions Court Judge Marlina Ibrahim deferred Paul Akang’s sentencing to Oct 28 this year pending medical and forensic reports. Pending the date, Paul was further remanded. Paul is accused of causing serious injury to the 45-year-old man by using the weapon at 5pm on Sept 21 this year in front of a house in Kg Kelansatan, Kuala Penyu. DPP Ronnie Antony prosecuted the case. Man freed of RM108,500 cheating charge Daily Express Daily Express Online (Malaysia) is Sabah's top-ranked & most viewed English news site. title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan 2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), berkata agihan pendapatan akhir bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 Sept 2026 adalah sebanyak 2.1 sen seunit, dengan tambahan agihan bonus sebanyak 0.4 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan PHB selaku penaja dana itu. “Edaran bonus itu akan diberikan bagi 1,000,000 unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Dengan mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.5 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan pada April 2026, jumlah keseluruhan agihan pendapatan AHB bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 2026 adalah lima sen seunit,” menurut kenyataan itu. PHB berkata sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan pada pusingan akhir, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan tahunan sebanyak RM236.41 juta. Pengarah Urusan kumpulan PHB Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan pendapatan bagi setahun penuh itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB yang berterusan serta kekuatan portfolio hartanah asasnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan yang berdisiplin oleh PHB. “Prestasi AHB tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit. “Pada masa sama, kami kekal memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan yang dinamik serta pengoptimuman portfolio yang berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan yang mampan danpenciptaan nilai jangka panjang,” katanya. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM Zulkifli Ishak berkata pengurus dana itu kekal fokus menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB berkata agihan pendapatan itu akan dibayar dalam bentuk unit AHB yang dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun AHB pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Okt 2026. Agihan tersebut akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, sekali gus membolehkan pemegang unit menambah pegangan unit serta berpotensi menikmati kesan pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. “Pelabur Bumiputera yang ingin melanggan AHB boleh berbuat demikian pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. “Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd,” katanya. – BERNAMA

title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit, pemegang unit terima RM236.41 juta bagi FY2026 - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan jumlah agihan pendapatan termasuk bonus sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026 (FY2026), dengan keseluruhan pembayaran RM236.41 juta yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Berhad (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Berhad (PHBAM), mengumumkan agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, menurut kenyataan PHB bersama hari ini. PHB selaku penaja dana turut mengisytiharkan edaran bonus sebanyak 0.40 sen seunit, menjadikan jumlah agihan bagi tempoh tersebut sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Bonus itu diberikan kepada pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Selepas mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April 2026, jumlah agihan bagi FY2026 mencapai 5.00 sen seunit. Agihan akhir itu membabitkan pembayaran RM120.13 juta. Agihan pendapatan tersebut adalah bersih selepas cukai dan zakat, membolehkan pemegang unit menerima jumlah penuh tanpa sebarang potongan atau tanggungan tambahan. Pembayaran akan dibuat dalam bentuk unit AHB dan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober 2026. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan bagi FY2026 mencerminkan ketahanan berterusan AHB dan kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset serta pelaburan yang berdisiplin. “Prestasi AHB pada tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit,” katanya. Beliau berkata PHB terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera melalui pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang. Menurut Mazuki, penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB yang diumumkan baru-baru ini memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. Beliau berkata AHB akan terus menyokong pembentukan kekayaan jangka panjang Bumiputera dan menjana nilai mampan kepada pemegang unit. Komitmen itu selaras dengan aspirasi Pelan Transformasi Ekonomi Bumiputera 2035 (PUTERA35) untuk memperkukuh penyertaan ekonomi, pemilikan dan pembentukan kekayaan Bumiputera. Agihan dilaburkan semula secara automatik Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM, Zulkifli Ishak berkata pihaknya kekal komited menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab supaya dana itu terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. Agihan pendapatan akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, menambah pegangan unit pelabur dan membolehkan mereka berpotensi menikmati manfaat pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. Unit tambahan akan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun tanpa memerlukan permohonan berasingan. Pelabur Bumiputera boleh melanggan AHB pada harga tetap RM1.00 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. Langganan boleh dibuat di cawangan pengedar sah AHB seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), AmBank Berhad, AmBank Islamic Berhad, Bank Islam Malaysia Berhad dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Berhad. Sejak ditubuhkan pada 2010, AHB telah mengagihkan sejumlah RM2.7 bilion pendapatan kepada pemegang unit Bumiputera.

title: 'MKH bakal dinyahsenarai selepas Batu Kawan kuasai 95.16% saham
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt – MKH Bhd bakal dinyahsenarai daripada Bursa Malaysia selepas Batu Kawan Bhd bersama anak syarikatnya, Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd serta pihak yang bertindak bersama mereka menguasai 95.16% saham syarikat pemaju hartanah itu.   Jumlah pegangan tersebut bersamaan 548.85 juta saham MKH setakat penutupan dagangan pada 30 Sept 2026, menurut kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bagi pihak Batu Kawan dan Whitmore.   Dengan pegangan yang sudah melepasi 90%, Batu Kawan dan Whitmore kini boleh mengambil alih baki saham MKH yang masih dipegang pemegang saham yang tidak menerima tawaran pengambilalihan tersebut.

'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan jumlah agihan pendapatan termasuk bonus sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026 (FY2026), dengan keseluruhan pembayaran RM236.41 juta yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Berhad (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Berhad (PHBAM), mengumumkan agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, menurut kenyataan PHB bersama hari ini. PHB selaku penaja dana turut mengisytiharkan edaran bonus sebanyak 0.40 sen seunit, menjadikan jumlah agihan bagi tempoh tersebut sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Bonus itu diberikan kepada pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Selepas mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April 2026, jumlah agihan bagi FY2026 mencapai 5.00 sen seunit. Agihan akhir itu membabitkan pembayaran RM120.13 juta. Agihan pendapatan tersebut adalah bersih selepas cukai dan zakat, membolehkan pemegang unit menerima jumlah penuh tanpa sebarang potongan atau tanggungan tambahan. Pembayaran akan dibuat dalam bentuk unit AHB dan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober 2026. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan bagi FY2026 mencerminkan ketahanan berterusan AHB dan kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset serta pelaburan yang berdisiplin. “Prestasi AHB pada tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit,” katanya. Beliau berkata PHB terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera melalui pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang. Menurut Mazuki, penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB yang diumumkan baru-baru ini memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. title: 'Maybank upgrades MAE Malware Shielding to detect more security risks
body: 'Maybank is rolling out an enhanced version of its Malware Shielding feature on the MAE app, which can now detect a wider range of potential security risks on users’ devices. As part of the update, MAE users will also be required to review and agree to a new set of Malware Shielding Terms & Conditions before they can continue using the app  The upgraded feature started rolling out progressively on 26 September 2026 with MAE app version 0.9.51, so don’t be surprised if the update hasn’t reached your phone just yet. Once updated, you’ll be prompted to review and agree to the new terms before you can continue using the app. By tapping ‘Agree’, you’re acknowledging that Malware Shielding will check your device for potential malware and risky security settings every time you launch MAE.  So what exactly is it looking out for? According to Maybank, Malware Shielding can detect malicious apps that may intercept authentication codes, remotely control your device or steal banking credentials. It also checks for unsafe device configurations, including Developer Mode, rooted or jailbroken devices, emulators and cloned environments.  The feature can also detect active screen sharing, recording, mirroring and overlay apps, as well as VPN services and untrusted keyboard apps. On top of that, it checks whether the MAE app itself has been modified or tampered with.  As for privacy, Maybank says Malware Shielding does not access, collect, process or store any personal information from the apps installed on your device. The bank also says your banking information and personal data remain confidential and protected.

title: 'Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively. The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650 million tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. "The relevant reset distribution rates for the three tranches are based on the prevailing five-year, seven-year and 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rates, respectively, plus their respective initial spreads for fixed rates of 0.98 per cent, 0.97 per cent and 0.98 per cent per annum," said Maybank. The proceeds would be used for shariah-compliant purposes, including investments in ringgit- and foreign currency-denominated Islamic financial instruments approved by Bank Negara Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council or the Securities Commission Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council. It would also be used to fund the Islamic business activities of Maybank's subsidiaries and overseas branches, as well as other shariah-compliant business activities, said Maybank. The returns from the investments would be used for the periodic distributions of the AT1 sukuk mudharabah, which are payable semi-annually. The sukuk has been assigned an AA3 rating by RAM Rating Services Bhd.

title: 'Penangan BTS! Army Sanggup Beratur Awal Pagi Di Cawangan Maybank Untuk Dapatkan Kad Debit Edisi Terhad
body: 'Sekilas  Peminat BTS sanggup beratur awal pagi di cawangan terpilih Maybank untuk mendapatkan kad debit edisi terhad kumpulan itu. Hanya 60 keping kad ditawarkan setiap hari, tetapi Maybank juga menyediakan permohonan secara dalam talian bermula 28 September. Kad debit ini adalah sebahagian daripada kerjasama Maybank dengan siri jelajah dunia BTS, WORLD TOUR ARIRANG.  Penangan kumpulan terkenal Korea Selatan iaitu BTS memang tidak dapat disangkal apabila peminat kumpulan itu dilihat sanggup beratur dari awal pagi di beberapa cawangan Maybank bagi mendapatkan kad debit edisi terhad kumpulan berkenaan.  Meskipun hanya 60 keping kad ditawarkan setiap hari di cawangan terpilih, namun itu tidak menghalang golongan Army dari mendapatkan kad edisi terhad tersebut.  Bagi yang tidak berkesempatan untuk beratur, Maybank turut menyediakan pilihan permohonan secara dalam talian yang akan dibuka mulai 28 September ini.  Kad debit edisi terhad tersebut merupakan sebahagian daripada kerjasama Maybank bersempena siri jelajah dunia BTS yang akan datang, WORLD TOUR ARIRANG.  Kerjasama tersebut sekali gus memberi peluang kepada peminat BTS untuk memiliki kad debit khas yang menampilkan elemen berkaitan kumpulan tersebut.

title: 'Maybank limits BTS world tour debit card to 60 per branch per day, online applications open 28 September
body: 'Subscribe to our FREE Newsletter, or Telegram and WhatsApp channels for the latest stories and updates.  Maybank dropped the limited-edition Maybank Visa BTS World Tour “ARIRANG” Debit Card at 12 selected branches yesterday, and just as expected, fans queued up in droves to get their hands on it!  The new black card has a simple design, with the words “BTS World Tour ARIRANG” printed in a glossy finish across the bottom half of the card. It was released in conjunction with the Kpop band’s upcoming world tour.  Fans who braved the queues outside the banks proudly shared pictures of their new cards online. It’s easy to see why the excitement is so real because only 60 cards are issued per day at each selected Maybank branch, making this a seriously hot commodity.  If you don’t have time to queue, you can still get your hands on the Maybank BTS card online via Maybank2U from 28 September onwards. Simply open the Maybank2U app, go to “Settings,” select “Cards,” then choose “Replace/Renew Card.” Do note that this process comes with a card replacement fee of RM12.  Excitement for BTS-themed cards abroad  Malaysian fans are not the only ones treated to a special BTS bank card. Fans in Thailand and the Philippines have also shared their respective country’s card designs online — a sign of just how deeply the group has embedded itself across Southeast Asia.  That footprint runs especially deep in Malaysia. BTS has consistently sold out arenas here since their early tour years, with Malaysian ARMY widely regarded as one of the most organised and vocal fandoms in the region. The group’s blend of polished choreography, emotionally direct lyrics, and members who have spoken openly about mental health resonated strongly with young Malaysians navigating similar pressures. The fact that a national bank is now issuing limited-edition BTS debit cards is, in many ways, just the financial sector catching up to what fans already knew.  An Indonesian fan on X, formerly Twitter, expressed hope that local banks would release a BTS-themed card — or at minimum, a Flazz card, an e-money smart card issued by Bank Central Asia. The comment drew significant engagement, suggesting the appetite extends well beyond Malaysia’s borders.  Share your thoughts with us via TRP’s Facebook, X, Instagram, or Threads.

title: 'M’sians Camp Outside Maybank From 4am For BTS Card, Turning It Into Mini ‘Concert’ | WeirdKaya
body: 'What time would you wake up for a debit card? For some Malaysian BTS fans, apparently before the sun even comes up. Fans were seen gathering outside Maybank’s Shah Alam Main Branch in Seksyen 14 from the early hours of the morning after the Maybank Visa | BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ Debit Card became available on Sept. 23. And judging from the crowd, you might have mistaken the bank for a BTS concert venue. Fans arrived as early as 4am A staff member shared photos of the situation on Threads, showing BTS fans waiting both inside and outside the Shah Alam branch. In one post, he jokingly asked: Is this a bank or a BTS concert?” Speaking to WeirdKaya, Irfan confirmed that the scenes were taken at the Shah Alam Main Branch in Seksyen 14. According to him, customers had already begun showing up at around 3am to 4am. And the excitement did not stop after the first day. Day 2 also saw fans ‘camping’ outside In another update the following morning, Irfan shared a photo showing a group of customers sitting outside the bank while waiting for it to open. “Pagi ni pun ramai betul dah camping depan bank eh 😂,” he wrote. The photo showed fans sitting along the walkway with their bags and belongings, looking more like they were waiting for concert doors to open than preparing for a banking transaction. Once inside, the BTS energy continued. Photos shared by Irfan showed a packed banking hall, with customers holding BTS themed items while staff attended to the crowd. title: 'High-flying Miyu of Japan and Thai darling Jeeno Thitikul lead a world-class field of champions at the 2026 Maybank Championship
body: 'The Maybank Championship is set for another star-studded chapter when Asia’s premier ladies’ golf event returns to Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) this October 29-November 1. With a US$3 million prize purse, the fourth edition brings together Major champions, LPGA Tour winners and Southeast Asia’s emerging talents for four days of world-class competition at KLGCC. The competition for the coveted Tiger Trophy has never been more intense. Defending champion and Major winner Miyu Yamashita of Japan is one of the season's most in-form players, highlighted by a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada in August and a playoff win at the Sony JLPGA Championship in Japan in September. Having claimed a dramatic three-way playoff victory at last year’s Maybank Championship, she will have every intention of becoming the tournament’s first repeat champion. Crowd favourite, Thai darling and World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand is also on a rich vein of form, having already claimed three LPGA Tour victories in 2026 to take her total title tally to ten. She returns for a fourth consecutive year in pursuit of the elusive Tiger Trophy, having narrowly missed out in each of her last appearances. Thitikul’s close friend Ruoning Yin of China, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner and a Major champion, will also return to Malaysia in winning mode having triumphed at the FM Championship in August. The spotlight will also firmly be turned on Korean ace Haeran Ryu, who is currently second on the LPGA Tour’s Race to CME Globe ranking on the back of successive Major victories in 2026 at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship and the Amundi Evian Championship. Adding her considerable star power to the field is the perennially popular New Zealander Lydia Ko, a three-time Major winner and reigning Olympic champion who was inducted into the LPGA Hall of Fame in 2024 at age 27. Australian stalwart Hannah Green and Hye-Jin Choi of South Korea, who were the two other protagonists in last year's playoff, will return with unfinished business on their agendas. 2023 Maybank Championship winner Céline Boutier of France, who edged Thitikul in a nail-biting nine-hole playoff at KLGCC three years ago, is also in the field. Other fan favourites who have signed up include emerging English sensation Lottie Woad and her experienced compatriot Charley Hull, and Japanese twins Aki and Chizzy Iwai. The identical twins have been in roaring form this season and will be among the frontrunners for the title. The Maybank Championship is more than Asia’s premier golf event. It provides a distinctive regional pathway for Southeast Asian talent to earn their place alongside the world’s best. This year, five players who earned their places through the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier bring that story to life. Held in August at KLGCC’s West Course, the 36-hole qualifier concluded with Thai professional Pimnipa Panthong and her amateur compatriots Sarisa Pojanalai and Achiraya Sriwong locked together at four-under-par 140 (Sriwong turned professional recently). Standout Thai amateur Marisa Tojai, who had already claimed four amateur titles in 2026 before arriving at the qualifier, secured the fourth spot at two-under 142, while Malaysia’s Liyana Durisic rounded out the top five at one-under 143. For Malaysian fans, there will be plenty to roar about. Liyana Durisic is currently in great form, having already claimed four PGM Tour titles in 2026, and the Women’s World Sand Greens Championship held in Australia in March. She will be joined by a talented and recognisable group of Malaysian players entering as Sponsor’s Invitations, namely Mirabel Ting, Jeneath Wong, Natasha Oon and Kelly Tan, to make up a five-strong Malaysian challenge. 2025 Annika Award winner Mirabel Ting made headlines in 2024 by becoming the highest-finishing Malaysian in Maybank Championship history, with a T12 finish as an amateur. Her fine performances continued into her debut season on this year’s Epson Tour, helping her clinch two victories in 2026. The wins propelled Ting to the top of the Epson Tour’s Race for the Card standings and secured her place on the LPGA Tour for the 2027 season. Joining Ting is Malaysia’s highest-ranked amateur (currently ranked 59th), Jeneath Wong. After a stellar season in 2023 that saw her earn her a major championship start at the US Women's Open, Wong made history as the first Malaysian to win the Women's Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship in 2025, a victory which earned her further major championship starts, bringing an increasingly impressive international résumé to KLGCC. One-time Epson Tour winner and 2023 Epson Tour Rookie of the Year Natasha Oon makes her first appearance at the Maybank Championship since 2023, seeking to capitalise on her encouraging performance at the recent CPKC Women’s Open. The LPGA Tour rookie is rebuilding her momentum following a lengthy injury that saw her miss most of the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Completing the Malaysian line-up is two-time Olympian Kelly Tan, Malaysia's most successful LPGA Tour player. Tan recorded her career-best results on the LPGA Tour with runner-up finishes at the Dow Great Lakes Bay Invitational in 2022 and 2023, and returns to KLGCC for the third time, bringing over a decade of elite professional experience on the West Course.
